News.title: Suicide drones SWARM Moscow as Trump meets Zelensky & North Korea sends 30k more troops to boost desperate Putin’s ranks
News.content:
UKRAINE unleashed a swarm of suicide drones on Moscow hours before Volodymyr Zelensky and Donald Trump are due to meet today.

Nearly 400 unmanned aircraft overwhelmed the sky over Russia’s capital and the wider region – as mayor Sergei Sobyanin claimed that “most” had been intercepted.



Flames engulfed a logistics warehouse at Podolsk, and an apartment block in Chekhov was also hit.

The strike in Podolsk on the e 3PL logistics company was close to a massive warehouse belonging to Wildberries – Russia’s version of Amazon – which appeared undamaged.



While Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian retail warehouses as well as large oil refineries, the war-torn country is running out of desperately-needed air defence.

The Ukrainian President is expected to use his White House visit to press his US counterpart



Amid improving relations with US President Donald Trump he will seek tougher sanctions against Putin.

Zelensky is also calling for urgent anti-ballistic defence missiles to protect Ukrainians from Russian attack.

“Our top priority is anti-ballistic defence and strategic cooperation with America. Peace must come closer,” he said.

At a previous meeting in Washington in October 2025, Zelensky failed to convince Trump to provide Ukraine with Tomahawk cruise missiles.



And during heated exchanges in the Oval Office in February that year, both raised their voices during an argument in the full glare of television cameras.

The US leader has since changed his tone and during their last encounter in Turkey earlier this month, he offered words of encouragement, saying he had done “an amazing job”.

It comes as North Korea reaffirmed its support for Russia’s war on Ukraine as the nations’ foreign ministers met in Moscow.

Russia reportedly plans to enlist 30,000 North Korean soldiers for a full offensive in Ukraine, Zelesky said over the weekend.

But it is not the first time Ukrainian officials have sounded the alarm on the nations cooperation.



Pyongyang has sent troops to Russia’s embattled Kursk region and supplied Moscow with weapons systems, in return securing financial assistance, food, energy supplies and military technology, analysts say.

Kim Jong Un last travelled to Russia in September 2023, and Putin made a rare visit to Pyongyang in June 2024.

News.title: Moment French warship fires ‘intimidation’ shots near top Tory MP in the Channel during migrant surge
News.content:
SHOTS FIRED! Moment French warship fires ‘intimidation’ shots near top Tory MP in the Channel during migrant surge

A FRENCH warship fired “intimidation” shots near the Shadow Home Secretary in the Channel this morning.

Tory MP Chris Philp was out at sea monitoring small boat migrant crossings when the gunboat unleashed a barrage of ammunition.



He was in the middle of filming a broadcast interview when the crack of 17 live rounds could suddenly be heard.

Mr Philp said: “On the Channel today monitoring illegal migrant crossings. As I was being interviewed by the BBC just now a French warship approached close and fired 17 live rounds behind us.



“There was no notice or training exercise in place. Felt like warning shots or attempted intimidation.”

The French warship was seen close to Mr Philp’s fishing boat in the international shipping lane.

The French Navy, which helps patrol the Channel, has not yet responded to Mr Philp’s allegation.

Warm weather has seen a spike in small boat crossings with more than 900 making the journey last week.

The French Navy often escorts the crammed dinghies from the shallows into British waters where they are then picked up by Border Force.

Mr Philp’s allegations could spark a fresh diplomatic incident with France amid years of tensions in the Channel.



Britain is also paying France close to £1billion pounds for its help stopping illegal migration.

Home Office figures show 881 arrived in Dover since crossings resumed on Wednesday after days of windy conditions — including 165 on a 42ft-long mega-dinghy.

It beat the record of 128 for the most migrants getting here from France on one vessel.

The Home Office said: “We are bearing down on small boat crossings, with removals at record levels and asylum claims down by 12 per cent. We have removed or deported almost 70,000 people who were here illegally — an increase of 41 per cent.”

News.title: Two women in hospital with ‘life-altering’ injuries after triple stabbing near shopping centre as three arrested
News.content:
STAB HORROR Two women in hospital with ‘life-altering’ injuries after triple stabbing near shopping centre as three arrested

TWO women have been left with “potentially life-altering” injuries after a triple stabbing near a shopping centre.

Police were called to reports that three people had been stabbed in a flat on Wasnidge Walk, Nottingham, before jumping from a window together.



Two women and a man were injured in the horror with the two women rushed to hospital for treatment.

The man was located outside the flat, while the two women were found with injuries in Nottingham city centre.



All three people – a 27-year-old man and two women, aged 26 and 31 – have since been arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm.

The trio remain in hospital at this time with the women’s injuries described as potentially life-altering but not currently life-threatening.

Nottinghamshire Police has now launched an investigation into the incident adding that the incident posed to wider risk to the public.

The force is now appealing for any information that may assist their probe into the horror.

Chief Inspector Kylie Davies, of Nottinghamshire Police, said: “We are still in the early stages of our investigation into this complex incident, but can confirm that three suspects have now been arrested.

“All three are currently receiving treatment in hospital, having appeared to have sustained stab wounds and other injuries at various stages of this incident, which was isolated and poses no threat to the wider public.



“We’re still trying to piece together exactly what happened here, so in the meantime, we’d ask people to please share any information they have, however small or insignificant it may seem.

“In addition to anyone who witnessed this take place, we also want to hear from anyone who has CCTV, doorbell, dash-cam, or mobile phone footage that could assist our ongoing inquiries.”

People can share information by contacting Nottinghamshire Police on 101, quoting incidents 773 and 781 of July 27.

News.title: Notorious women’s jail plagued with violence launches competition with bizarre prize in desperate bid to curb attacks
News.content:
GUILTY AS CHARRED Notorious women’s jail plagued with violence launches competition with bizarre prize in desperate bid to curb attacks

WINNERS of a violence-reduction competition will be treated to fakeaways in a women’s prison, according to a new report.

Inmates at HMP Foston Hall, a 320-capacity women’s jail in Derbyshire, can tuck into specially-made meals by kitchen staff as a reward for not fighting each other or staff.



Among the most popular fakeaways – homemade takeaway foods – include curries, fish and chips, Chinese meals, tacos, pizzas, burgers, and even kebabs.

The jail has seven wings – each holding between 30-60 inmates – but only one wing can be the monthly winner.



Kitchen workers are then tasked with rustling up the ‘special’ dishes for those on the wing with the best record for non-violence.

The infamous lock-up currently houses the likes of Lorraine Thorpe, one of Britain’s youngest female double murderers, convicted in 2010 at the age of 15.



And also Louise Porton, convicted in 2019 of murdering her two young daughters.

The prison has previously held the likes of Moors murderer Myra Hindley, Soham murderer Ian Huntley‘s ex Maxine Carr and Karen Matthews, jailed for her role in the high-profile fake kidnapping plot of her own daughter Shannon in 2008.



The plan was revealed in the most recent report by inspectors from the Independent Monitoring Board (IMB), released last month, which said jail chiefs had implemented the scheme to deal with a rising tide of violence.

They said that attacks on staff were up 21% and inmate scraps were up 11% in the past year – and that the ‘fakeaways’ treats were aimed at drastically reducing the number of attacks.

Results are due out later this year on whether it’s worked or not.



The report by inspectors from the Independent Monitoring Board (IMB) stated that the initiative was supported by the introduction of ‘peacekeepers’ – trusted red band lags – who try to intervene before things get ugly.

The IMB report states: “There have been new initiatives to encourage positive behaviour, including a monthly reward for the wing with the lowest levels of violence, with a ‘fakeaway’ – takeaway food from the kitchen.

“The introduction of a peer mentor as a ‘peacekeeper’ to help resolve low-level disagreements has been another positive step.”

The IMB also said the quality of the food served up was enjoyed by most lags – and even themselves.

It stated: “The IMB has regularly observed food being prepared in the kitchens and noted that it looked appetising, was well presented and tasted good when sampled.



“In the IMB general survey, 65% of respondents said the food was good or reasonable.”

The report also praised the jail for its well-kept gardens, hairdressing salon, and gym.

It said, however, the outside playing field was ‘uneven’ and not safe to play sports on.

It stated: “The exterior environment is pleasant, with well-kept gardens, an animal sanctuary, a textile workshop, hairdressing salon, gym and large playing field.

“The latter (however) is considered unsafe to use for team games owing to its uneven surface.”



Prison bosses say the report showed that ‘front-line staff’ at the jail were doing a good job, but that it was aware there was ‘ongoing challenges’ faced by staff.

It comes after inspectors last year reported the jail continued to be affected by high levels of violence self-harm and unacceptable behaviour from staff.

HM Inspectorate of Prisons (HMIP) released its findings in April 2025 following an unannounced inspection the previous January.

It led to the prison’s governor launching an action plan, according to the Prison Service.

A spokesperson for HMIP told the BBC: “Although violence was rarely serious and violence against staff was falling, the number of violent incidents remained the highest in the women’s estate.



“Self-harm was also too high, despite a fall in incidents.

“Inconsistent care and a lack of assistance from staff were compounding the problems and causing women frustration.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Prison Service spokesperson said: “This scheme is designed to encourage good behaviour, reducing violence and keeping staff safe.

“All food is made within the prison kitchen and is never brought in from outside.”

News.title: Second Brit tourist, 54, dies after 20ft plunge when wooden bannister collapsed at holiday resort in Lanzarote
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

DEADLY PLUNGE Second Brit tourist, 54, dies after 20ft plunge when wooden bannister collapsed at holiday resort in Lanzarote

A SECOND British tourist has died almost a year after the two holidaymakers fell over 20ft after a bannister collapsed in Lanzarote.

Nicholas Thomas, 54, tragically died in hospital months after suffering terminal injuries at a holiday resort in the Canary Islands.



Thomas succumbed to his injuries after nearly ten months in hospital.

He and his friend, 56-year-old Darren Silcox also from Cwmbran, Gwent, fell into an atrium stairwell at the Galeon Playa Apartments in Costa Teguise on October 25.



The pair fell between 15-22ft after a wooden banister “collapsed” on their balcony, an inquest heard.

Silcox was pronounced dead at the scene.



Thomas’s family were told by doctors in October that he may never recover.

He was transferred to University Hospital Llandough, near Cardiff, in November but sadly died on July 10.



The inquest into Silcox’s death heard he died from traumatic brain injury, skull fractures and skull lacerations.

The proceedings were adjourned until April 14 next year when a joint inquest is expected to be held.

Following Silcox’s passing, local councillor David Daniels said he was a “great guy”.



Silcox was a much-loved shopkeeper who owned two stores in Pontnewydd and Five Locks.

One shopper said: “This is terrible.

“It is a family store and everyone knows them – what a shocking way to go.

“He was always very hard working.”

Locals say his wife Kim died a year after an illness. One said: “They have two children who are now left without parents – it is tragic.”



Spain‘s Civil Guard has launched a probe into the circumstances surrounding the incident which happened on October 25.

Back in 2023, an 18-year-old also died after falling from a balcony at Galeon Playa Apartment-Hotel.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

David Alexander plunged from the balcony while on holiday with his family.

Heartbroken friends and family have remembered him as a “much-loved and respected” college student.

News.title: Secret new Israeli intel on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuke lair ‘to be shared with Trump’ as war’s fate hangs in balance
News.content:
SECRET new Israeli intelligence on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain nuclear lair will be shared with Donald Trump, according to reports.

The US president is set to meet with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu today to discuss the war and the Islamic Republic’s nuclear programme.



During the meeting Netanyahu’s team will hand over evidence of Iran’s latest nuclear activity, a source in Jerusalem told the New York Post.

On Monday Trump announced negotiations with Tehran were back on after days of strikes, but the bombshell revelation could reignite full-scale war.



Israel believes Iran has moved thousands of uranium-enrichment centrifuges into tunnels deep inside Pickaxe Mountain, officials told the Wall Street Journal.

The regime allegedly made the transfer after the 12-day war in June 2025, when US and Israeli strikes pummelled Iran’s three main nuclear sites.



Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan were all blitzed by “massive ordnance penetrator” bombs in the operation called “Midnight Hammer”.

Pickaxe Mountain lair lies more than 300 feet beneath Kolang Mountain near the Natanz nuclear facility.



The site is heavily fortified, and it is believed to hosts two tunnel complexes.

The head of the UN’s nuclear watchdog said last year: “It is obvious it is in a place where numerous and important activities related to the programme are taking place.”

When asked what was going on beneath Pickaxe, Iran responded: “It’s none of your business.”

Satellite images previously revealed tunnels feeding into the mountain and leading to a deep-buried operation.

Experts say it could be more secure than any of the facilities struck by the US and Israel.



Trump has previously left the site untouched while bombing Iran’s other major nuclear bunkers.

But last week he warned the US would strike the area “pretty soon” and “very heavily.”

Responding to claims by Israel that the Islamic Republic has concealed its stockpiles in the mountain, he said: “I think that they may have. We don’t have it on record.“



During today’s meeting Israel is also expected to expose evidence that Iran is rebuilding its missile and drone program.

It comes as Trump paused a nearly two-week-long bombing campaign on Iran over the weekend as fresh talks began to end Tehran’s attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

He seemed hopeful for an end to the war on Monday, telling reporters aboard Air Force One: “I think there’s a good chance that something could happen.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But, he warned Washington would “go back to doing what we were doing” before the pause in fighting if the latest negotiations failed.

Tehran has denied that any direct negotiations are taking place.

News.title: Top Gear star Richard Hammond slapped with £999 fine after being clocked speeding in Bentley & Porsche
News.content:
PAYING THE PRICE Top Gear star Richard Hammond slapped with £999 fine after being clocked speeding in Bentley & Porsche

TOP Gear star Richard Hammond has been slapped with a £999 fine after he was clocked speeding twice.

The TV presenter, 56, was caught behind the wheel of a Porsche in December last year and then caught again driving a Bentley just 20 days later.



West Mercia Police have brought two prosecutions against Hammond with speed camera images of him driving the swanky motors in Herefordshire as evidence.

A police officer operating a handheld speeding camera caught the TV personality speeding just before 1pm on December 2 last year.



His Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo was clocked at 68mph in a 50mph limit on the A40 in Pencraig, Herefordshire.

At around 11.45am on December 22, Hammond’s Bentley Continental GT was speeding at 82mph in a 70mph limit on the A50 Rudhall Overbridge in Herefordshire.

Court documents also show officers spent weeks trying to notify the Grand Tour host.

Several letters regarding the offences were sent to his multi-million-pound portfolio of homes in a bid to track him down.



Police sent speeding tickets to a Grade II listed Herefordshire castle bought by Hammond in 2012.

They also sent letters to £1 million farm estate near Hereford, but the letters were returned from both addresses marked as “addressee gone away.”

Eventually, cops tracked the star down at his £2 million mansion near Abergavenny in Wales.

It was noted more than 30 vehicles are currently registered at the address.

Hammond, who worked alongside Jeremy Clarkson and James May on Top Gear and The Grand Tour, has pleaded guilty to two charges of speeding through his lawyers.



Police also set out in court papers that Hammond had been accused of another driving offence in August last year.

Hammond was prosecuted for two offences of speeding and two further allegations that he had ignored the police letters and failed to identify himself as the guilty driver.

In a letter to the court, the presenter’s solicitor pleaded guilty to the speeding charges and denied the other two offences.

The letter read: “He replied identifying himself as the driver. He sent the reply by First Class post. He posted the reply himself.”

The police force opted to withdraw those extra charges, as Hammond was prosecuted and convicted for the speeding offences in the Single Justice Procedure.



Last week at Telford Magistrates Court he was slapped with seven penalty points on his licence.

Magistrate Ann Minton also ordered the TV personality to pay a total fine of £1,771.

The lump sum was made up of two fines of £333 and £666 as well as £240 in costs and victim surcharges totalling £532.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nicknamed The Hamster by his co-hosts, Hammond almost died in a 320mph jet car crash in 2006 while filming Top Gear.

He also received a three-month driving ban in France alongside Clarkson in 2013 when they were caught speeding while filming an episode of the show.

News.title: Disinherited nephew who threatened to ‘beat the s**t’ out of ‘w****r’ lawyers after aunt left £200k to charity is jailed
News.content:
FAMILY FEUD Disinherited nephew who threatened to ‘beat the s**t’ out of ‘w****r’ lawyers after aunt left £200k to charity is jailed

A DISINHERITED nephew who threatened to “beat the s**t” out of “w****r” lawyers” after his aunt left her £200,000 estate to charity.

Dr Sean Stimson, 48, was also slapped with a £35,000 court bill following a bitter row over the will of his late aunt, Helen Smith.



The IT expert became “extremely emotionally involved” in the dispute after his “very close” aunt left her estate to the RSPCA and other charities under a 2016 will.

But Dr Stimson was adamant she had always intended her home on Cloudberry Road, Swindon – which made up most of the value of the estate – to stay in the family.



He is still disputing the will, but has now been put behind bars for contempt of court and ordered to pay legal costs after writing an email and letter to the charities’ lawyers, Foot Anstey LLP.

London’s High Court heard how the enraged nephew wrote to the law firm, addressing them as “w****rs” and “b*****s” and threatened to “beat the “s**t” out of them if the house was not returned to him.



Mr Justice Griffiths yesterday handed him an immediate jail term of 28 days, saying that he had aggravated his two contempts of court by stating afterwards that he “thought he would get away with it because jails are full”.

The judge also ordered Dr Stimson to pay the law firm’s £35,000 costs of bringing the contempt proceedings against him.



Lawyers for the firm had told the court that the “abuse” in the email and the letter put Dr Stimson in contempt of court twice by breaching a previous order banning him from such conduct.

The order had settled a Foot Anstey harassment claim against him last year.

In a previous judgment on the dispute between Dr Stimson and the law firm, High Court judge Mrs Justice Hill set out the background to the row explaining: “His aunt left a will made in 2016 which made provision for three animal charities and a hospice to recover under her estate.

“It made no provision for Dr Stimson and this led to a dispute between him and Foot Anstey, who are the administrators of the estate, instructed by the beneficiary charities.”

Dr Stimson disputed his aunt’s will on grounds that she lacked sufficient mental capacity and understanding to make her 2016 will, also claiming that another later will of 2020 set out her true wishes about her £200,000 home.



But Mrs Justice Hill said that, on the evidence she had seen, he had not been able to “substantiate these assertions” and since then probate has been granted to the charities involved.

He has continued to dispute the validity of the will, but ended up in court after Foot Anstey accused him of a campaign of harassment against them.

He was accused of threatening to turn up at the firm’s and charities’ offices, of threatening to spread malware in their IT systems, and of “making obscene phone calls to female employees.”

Dr Stimson, who denied making any obscene phone calls, ended up settling the harassment claim with Foot Anstey in January 2025 which only permitted him to contact the firm on “bona fide” issues relating to his aunt’s estate.

Foot Anstey’s barrister, Kate Wilson, asked for him to be jailed, accusing him of breaching the terms with communications sent in June and September last year.



An email sent in June referred to an appeal he was bringing in relation to his aunt’s will and concluded: “My aunt’s last wishes were very clear, and they will not be ignored and if necessary defended by force.”

The barrister claimed: “Then in September, his threatening conduct became more serious, when he made another threat of violence towards Foot Anstey’s staff if they did not ‘return’ his aunt’s house to him.”

The letter was “abusively addressed” to “Dear Foot Anstey W****rs” and read: “I am giving you one week to return my aunt’s house and bury her properly.

“If not I will come and beat the s**t out of all of you including the b*****s. I have had enough of your cr*p and the jails are full so I will just keep coming for you until you comply or are permanently hospitalised.”

Ms Wilson said the “b*tches” reference was especially troubling as the staff members who had worked on the charity will dispute were women.



The letter was a “clear breach of the undertakings” and contained a “direct threat”, the barrister argued, adding: “the vitriolic nature of that abuse added to the intensity of the threats of violence”.

Dr Stimson, fighting the contempt application, admitted sending an email to say his case would be “defended with force,” but claimed he was referring to legal force not physical violence.

He also claimed that he had nothing to do with the “w*****s” letter, accusing the law form of having printed it off and sent it to themselves.

His barrister Daniel Mullin, arguing that he ought not to be jailed, said he was “extremely emotionally involved in the underlying proceedings,” adding: “The start of all this was the death of someone who appears to have been very close to him.”

But sentencing him yesterday, Mr Justice Griffiths said: “The letter was more threatening than the email. It was understood to threaten grievous bodily harm against the claimant’s staff…. He did mean a threat of unlawful force.”



The firm had implemented “increased security measures” at their office due to the letter, he said, adding: “That was a reasonable step”.

“The letter was not fired off on the spur of the moment,” the judge said, adding that Dr Stimson had compounded the seriousness of the contempt by later saying that he “didn’t care about it and would get away with it because jails are full,” and by claiming that the law firm had sent the letter to themselves.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Saying that he was due no credit for admitting his contempt or showing any remorse, the judge concluded: “Although I recognise that he was very deeply invested in the legacy dispute…the balance is clearly against suspending the sentence.

“For the two contempts of court, I sentence Dr Stimson to 28 days’ immediate custody.”

News.title: Japan earthquake live: Panic in Kumamoto as buildings burn amid tsunami alert
News.content:
An urgent tsunami alert has been issued for the Ariake Bay area in Japan after a huge 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck the island of Kyushu

A powerful earthquake has hit Japan with buildings bursting into flames and an urgent tsunami alert issued. At least 50 people have been injured.

Japanese authorities issued the tsunami warning after the 7.1 magnitude quake rocked multiple towns in Kumamoto province on the southern Japanese island of Kyushu - where roughly 13million people live. The alert is for nearby Ariake bay on the western coasts of Kumamoto, about 900km (560mi) southwest of Tokyo.

The massive quake measured at the highest possible level seven on Japan's own Shindo "scale of shaking" and has left tens of thousands without power.

Kumamoto Airport has been closed indefinitely after the earthquake rocked its runway.

News.title: Meghan Markle’s MasterChef episode ratings soar despite mixed criticism from viewers
News.content:
Meghan Markle’s MasterChef episode ratings soar despite mixed criticism from viewers

Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, appeared on MasterChef Australia on Sunday night, and although watchers were divided in their opinion of her inclusion in the show, the episode broke records with its viewership

View 5 Images Meghan gave advice and critiques to contestants during her appearance on MasterChef as a guest judge (Image: Sunrise/Youtube)

Meghan Markle has broken records with her appearance on MasterChef Australia, with the episode raking up an impressive number of views. The Duchess of Sussex was a guest judge on the show, which aired on Sunday, where she guided contestants to create a dish ‘fit for a Duchess’.

The episode was filmed in April, when Harry and Meghan undertook a trip to Australia where they completed a series of engagements in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra. And while some viewers were divided over the Duchess’ inclusion in the cooking programme, more than one million people tuned in to watch the episode.

Disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor set to lose final honour after failing to respond to request READ MORE :

View 5 Images Meghan was a guest judge on MasterChef Australia (Image: Sunrise/Youtube)

More than 1.5 million people watched the show as it broke the record for the biggest overnight Sunday audience since July 2023 and the biggest-ever overnight streaming audience, according to figures released by broadcaster Network 10.

It also topped the seven-day total viewing audience with 1.22 million national viewers. Meghan’s episode saw a 16% increase in its national total TV audience compared with the same episode last year. Total TV is a special metric used in Australia to measure viewing across screens and combines traditional linear broadcast television with digital broadcast video-on-demand (BVOD) viewing.

5 View 5 Images The Duchess' episode broke viewing records (Image: 10/Masterchef) 5 View 5 Images Viewers were divided over Meghan's involvement in the episode (Image: 10/Masterchef)

The impressive viewing figures come as watchers shared their divided opinions online over Meghan’s involvement in the episode, given the guest judge position on the show is usually reserved for high-calibre chefs.

One viewer said: “It makes you feel a bit sorry for the contestants. They’ve gone on that show to learn from industry chefs, which Meghan is not. She’s a home cook, like the competitors are.”

Others, however, loved to see the Duchess on the programme, saying her calm energy and encouraging words were a nice change for the usually frantic MasterChef kitchen.

During the episode, Meghan spoke of her love of cooking, as she said to the contestants: "Food and cooking to me is really a love language."

View 5 Images Meghan filmed a guest spot on MasterChef Australia as part of their 'quasi-royal' tour

She continued: "I think it’s such a great way to connect. It’s something that can feel sentimental and meaningful and it's how I show my nurturing and love for my friends, family, and my kids."

Behind the scenes footage showed her smiling as she spoke to fellow judges and contestants. Meghan explained why she wanted to take part in the episode when her appearance was announced earlier this month.

She said: "What attracted me to the MasterChef Australia kitchen? Two things: my love of food and my love of Australia. It was an easy yes. It's such a great show. I'm just really honoured that I was asked to be able to be here with you and to be able to judge some of these meals."

News.title: Ryanair 'only offered to rebook flight' for passenger sucked out of window
News.content:
Ryanair 'only offered to rebook flight' for passenger sucked out of window

Serbian businessman Ljubisa Karovic, 61, was partially sucked out of a Ryanair plane window at 20,000ft when the window broke on a flight from Greece to Germany

View 2 Images Passenger Ljubisa Karović pictured with wife Svetlana Grković (Image: Facebook)

A Ryanair passenger who was partially sucked out of a plane window at 20,000ft has said the airline has done nothing except offer to rebook his flight following the terrifying ordeal.

‌



Ljubisa Karovic, 61, was nearly ripped from the aircraft when the window broke in mid-air on a flight from Thessaloniki in Greece to Memmingen near Munich, Germany, on July 10.

‌



His panicking wife Svetlana Grković told how she was forced to pull her husband back into the plane as he repeatedly lost consciousness during the horrifying emergency.

‌



Serbian businessman Ljubisa has been left wearing a neck brace for at least six weeks. He claimed no Ryanair officials have been in touch with him directly following the incident, which made headlines around the world.

View 2 Images The damaged window after the flight had landed

Ljubisa told the Daily Mail: “All we’ve had is emails to my son, who booked our flights, asking if we want to rebook and asking how I was. But nobody from the company has contacted me directly, not even a phone call to show any concern.”

‌



His wife Svetlana claimed cabin crew “didn’t do anything” and merely “looked scared” while other passengers battled to cling on to Ljubisa’s legs as he was sucked from the cabin.

Medical staff met the Boeing 737 on the tarmac after it made an emergency landing back at Thessaloniki airport, with Ljubisa rushed to hospital.

Passengers described a bang “like a tyre bursting” before the window ruptured.

Article continues below

The Mirror has contacted Ryanair for a comment.

Ryanair’s group chief financial officer Neil Sorahan previously said: “Our customer care team have actively been in touch with the family since the incident.

“Our crew did a phenomenal job and got the aircraft back to Thessaloniki. Everyone, bar none, walked off the aircraft. It was a great job done by the cabin crew and the pilots.”

News.title: France wildfires live: Thousands of tourists evacuated from coast near Bordeaux
News.content:
Flames are nearing the French Atlantic Coast with raging wildfires now nine miles from Bordeaux as the city's mayor says he's prepared for 'all eventualities'

A mass evacuation of tourists has been ordered from an area near the French Atlantic Coast as inferno wildfires burn nearby.

More than 4,000 people have been told to leave campsites, tourist homes, holiday villages and leisure parks around Lacanau, which is around 40 miles from Bordeaux.

The order comes as firefighters race against time to bring the fires under control before the country's south-west is blasted by a new 41C heatwave.

French President Emmanuel Macron says the wildfires are the "most difficult situation" his country has dealt with since World War Two, with more than 260,000 people now evacuated from their homes in the south-west.

The mayor of Bordeaux, Thomas Cazenave, says he is preparing for "all eventualities" and that authorities are preparing to "accommodate a large number of people should further evacuations be ordered".

Meanwhile in Spain, 63,000 people have been evacuate from their homes near Madrid, with the country's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez calling it "the most painful expression of the climate emergency".

News.title: King Charles' princess goddaughter marks 30th birthday with wild yacht party
News.content:
King Charles' princess goddaughter marks 30th birthday with wild yacht party

Princess Olympia of Greece, the goddaughter of King Charles, marked her 30th birthday over the weekend with a wild yacht party, which even saw her officially confirm she is no longer single

View 3 Images Princess Olympia, the goddaughter of King Charles, turned 30 over the weekend

Princess Maria-Olympia of Greece officially entered her thirties in style over the weekend, as she held a lavish yacht party for herself and her friends - including her boyfriend, who made his debut on her social media accounts.

‌



The model, who is the daughter of Greece's Crown Prince Pavlos and Princess Marie-Chantal and is the goddaughter of King Charles, turned 30 on Saturday (25th July), and spent all weekend celebrating in a variety of ways. On top of multiple yacht parties, photos shared online also seemed to show Olympia attending a family dinner organised by her parents, several clips of her dancing, and two separate birthday cakes.

‌



Olympia shared a series of snaps from her weekend adventures on Instagram, which seemed to show her kicking off her birthday festivities with a lavish get-together on a yacht. Another photo, shared by her father, showed the model posing in a grey bikini alongside both her parents.

‌



Another photo shared by Pavlos showed the blonde beauty cutting into a chocolate cake while sitting at a table on the yacht, where crystal blue water could be seen in the background alongside striking white cliffs.

View 3 Images Princess Olympia is the goddaughter of King Charles III (Image: Matteo Prandoni/BFA.com/REX/Shutterstock)

The Crown Prince captioned his photos: "Happy Birthday, dear Olympia, you are my sunshine."

‌



In a video shared by Olympia's mother, it was then confirmed that the princess's brothers, Achileas and Constantine Alexios, also joined in the celebrations, as they were seen carefully carrying a giant cake decorated with raspberries.

Olympia was filmed blowing out the candles on her cake while her guests, including Norwegian singer Peter Dundas, photographer Alexia Mavrolleon, and one of Olympia's long-term friends, Evangeline, all sang happy birthday to her.

View 3 Images Olympia debuted her boyfriend in her Instagram posts for her birthday (Image: olympiagreece/Instagram)

‌



Photos and videos shared on Olympia's own Instagram account then showed other lavish parties she attended over the weekend. In several clips, she can be seen dancing under flashing lights, posing with her friends, and having what appeared to be a karaoke session.

In one very short clip of Olympia posing at a party, her Argentinian businessman boyfriend, Martin Pacanowski, could be seen standing beside her. The couple were first linked together in 2024, but she has kept their romance private and never posted him on social media before her birthday event.

While Princess Olympia and the rest of her family continue to use their royal titles, Greece technically no longer has a royal family. Olympia's grandparents, Constantine II of Greece and Anne-Marie of Denmark, were the last King and Queen of the Hellenes, after the 1974 Greek public referendum voted to abolish the monarchy.

Article continues below

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Olympia's father is now the head of the family following the passing of Constantine II in 2023. While the model was born in New York, she and her family relocated to London when she was young, and she spent most of her childhood in the UK.

The family are very close to the British monarchy, as proven by King Charles, who at the time was Prince Charles, agreeing to be Olympia's godfather when she was born in 1996.

News.title: I gained four stone while eating 'healthily' - then I found out why
News.content:
I gained four stone while eating 'healthily' - then I found out why

Rebeca battled years of unexplained weight gain, fatigue and bloating

View 2 Images Rebeca underwent lots of tests but everything initially came back normal (Image: Supply Life)

A woman who endured years of relentless fatigue, agonising bloating and inexplicable weight gain says she finally feels like herself once more after finding out why.

‌



Rebeca Rodriguez, 38, from Elephant and Castle, London, had put on around four stone over the past decade despite making numerous attempts to enhance her wellbeing. She consumed what she thought was a well-rounded diet, exercised consistently, consulted three separate nutritionists and attended her GP on several occasions, frantic to understand why she felt so poorly.

‌



Yet, she was continually told that her blood test results were normal. "I knew something wasn't right," said Rebeca. "I was exhausted all the time, but every test kept coming back saying everything was fine."

‌



The sales director says her wellbeing hit rock bottom at the start of 2024, when even rising from bed became a challenge. She said: "There were days when I literally couldn't move. I'd wake up feeling exhausted before the day had even started. Some weeks I barely left my flat because I simply didn't have the energy."

Rebeca said she had grown so accustomed to feeling drained that she nearly accepted it as her reality. "I just thought this was adulthood. I thought maybe everyone felt like this."

Alongside the debilitating tiredness, she endured near-constant bloating and digestive distress, but never imagined that anything in her diet could be to blame. She said: "I genuinely believed it was normal to feel bloated after every meal.

‌



"I thought everybody passed gas after eating. It sounds ridiculous now, but because I'd lived with it for so long, I assumed that was just how digestion worked."

Doctors carried out a number of investigations, including repeated blood tests. "The only thing that ever really showed up was my white blood cell count," Rebeca explained.

"I was always told I was probably fighting off a virus or a cold because I seemed to pick up infections quite often, but nobody could explain why I constantly felt so drained." Despite her symptoms, Rebeca pressed on in her efforts to improve her wellbeing.

‌



View 2 Images Rebeca now feels much more like her old self (Image: Supply Life)

She ditched takeaways in favour of home-cooked meals, worked out more frequently and consulted three separate nutritionists, yet maintains that nothing appeared to make any real difference. "I wasn't looking for a quick fix or some miracle diet," she said. "I genuinely wanted to understand what was going on with my body."

Originally from Spain, Rebeca acknowledges that her increasing weight also took a toll on her self-esteem. She said: "In Spain there's a huge amount of pressure on women to look a certain way.

‌



"I've felt like I needed to lose weight since I was about 16. Every time I went home I became so conscious of how I looked."

She gradually lost her enthusiasm for clothes shopping, shied away from having her photograph taken, and felt progressively at odds with the sociable person she had always been. But everything shifted when a friend recommended she attempt a food intolerance test through Supply Life.

Rebeca confesses she was initially dubious, but claims the findings were utterly unexpected. She said: "I honestly couldn't believe it. Some of the foods highlighted were things I'd been eating almost every day because I thought they were healthy."

‌



Among the foods she reacted to were egg whites, potatoes, rice and yeast - everyday staples that had constituted a significant portion of her daily diet and numerous traditional Spanish dishes. "I remember looking at the results thinking, 'Well, there goes Spanish omelette... there goes paella,'" she said.

Rather than eggs for breakfast, Rebeca now typically enjoys avocado on sourdough toast with tomatoes. Lunch is generally a large salad with chicken, salmon or tuna, while dinner focuses on lean protein accompanied by vegetables, incorporating alternatives such as quinoa or couscous instead of rice where suitable.

Within weeks of altering her diet, she experienced something she hadn't felt for years. "My bloating almost disappeared," she said. "I had my first meal and afterwards I remember thinking, 'Is this what everyone else feels like?'. I felt comfortably full but I wasn't swollen or uncomfortable."

Article continues below

Increased energy and weight loss

As her digestion improved, her energy gradually started returning as well. She said: "I've gone from a size 18 to a size 16, and even those clothes are starting to feel loose now. But for me, the biggest change isn't the weight - it's having my energy back."

Rebeca says friends and family have also noticed the transformation. "They keep saying I've got my sparkle back," she said. "I've always been quite bubbly and positive, but I'd completely lost that version of myself. Now I feel like she's coming back."

Reflecting on her journey, she only wishes she'd recognised sooner that the symptoms she'd tolerated for years weren't something she simply had to endure. She said: "I spent such a long time thinking this was just my body. Now I realise you shouldn't ignore symptoms just because you've had them for years. I finally feel like myself again."

News.title: Plans to transform former KFC into 'Chicken Empathy Museum' - with slaughterhouse exhibits
News.content:
Plans to transform former KFC into 'Chicken Empathy Museum' - with slaughterhouse exhibits

Animal rights campaigners propose to transform a vacant former KFC in Fleetwood, Lancashire, into a "Chicken Empathy Museum", complete with slaughterhouse exhibits, vegan food and mascot chicken

View 2 Images PETA wants to see a change in the vacant former KFC (Image: Google)

A former KFC could swap fried chicken for feathers under an unusual new proposal from animal rights campaigners.

‌



People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) wants to transform the vacant takeaway in Fleetwood, Lancashire, into a “Chicken Empathy Museum” and has written to Landwood Property Auctions to ask whether the building’s owner would consider lending or donating the Lord Street site for educational use. The proposal comes after the former restaurant was put up for sale with a guide price of £100,000.

‌



Dawn Carr, PETA’s vice-president of vegan projects, said: “Turning a former KFC into a Chicken Empathy Museum would give this site a new purpose, one that encourages visitors to see chickens as the clever, curious individuals they are. PETA would be delighted to help transform a place once linked to suffering into one that inspires compassion.”

‌



View 2 Images The vacant property is currently on the market with a £100,000 guide price (Image: Getty Images)

Cruel owner made three dogs live in house of horror in smashed glass and broken furniture READ MORE :

Dad and UK champion dies in accident on holiday in Spain, aged 45 READ MORE :

If the charity gets its way, the former takeaway would be transformed into an attraction exploring chickens’ intelligence, emotions and social behaviour, alongside exhibits displaying equipment used in commercial poultry slaughterhouses, including kill cones and shackles. Visitors would also be able to meet PETA’s chicken mascot and sample vegan food.

‌



The animal rights organisation used the proposal as an opportunity to highlight its concerns within the poultry industry, claiming chickens are often kept in crowded sheds and selectively bred to grow rapidly before many develop health problems ahead of slaughter.

Ms Carr said: “Most people know chickens only as ‘nuggets’, ‘wings’, or ‘fillets’, yet these remarkable birds are intelligent, inquisitive individuals with their own unique personalities.

“They can recognise dozens of other chickens, communicate through a sophisticated range of vocalisations and even perform basic arithmetic. Mother hens talk to their chicks before they hatch and the chicks begin communicating back from inside the egg."

Article continues below

Neither the property’s owner nor Landwood Property Auctions had publicly responded to the proposal at the time of writing.

News.title: Love Island final LIVE: Jasmine addresses speculation she was fuming over Julia's win
News.content:
Tonight's final of Love Island will crown the 13th season's winners as Priya responds to 'job-shaming' allegations after Elicia comment

The Love Island has officially ended with Lorenzo Alessi and Julia Majchrzak announced as winners, beating out stiff competition from Kavan Murphy and Jasmine Muller.

However, it wasn't without drama as one Islander was noticeably absent from the proceedings, while fans were convinced that there was drama brewing between others.

Over the last few weeks, fans have voiced their belief that there was a row between Julia and Jas - which ramped up during last night's episode, as eagle-eyed viewers suggested that the latter snubbed her co-star over the win.

Social media users pored over the specific moment Maya announced the winners, where it seemed as though the Islanders ignored each other and failed to hug during the celebrations.

Jas was quick to squash the claims in her Debrief interview, telling hosts Shakira, Toni and Yasmin: “It’s so funny because in here - you guys know - it feels like such a big deal and then the minute you’re hanging out, it’s so minor and everything is minor.

“She’s actually iconic as hell, so we’re good.”

Here's everything else that went down as the new champions were crowned...

News.title: Schools to offer technical subjects from age 14 in England, Burnham says
News.content:
Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlined by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The government said the courses, which would be available from Year 10, would be linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.

Data published this year showed more than one million young people across the UK were not in education, employment or training, the highest level in more than 12 years.

Few details have been published about how the new vocational courses would work in practice and it is not clear how they would operate in areas with low industrial activity.

The BBC understands that the government expects the new pathways into work to be up and running in some areas by 2028.

Speaking at a train manufacturing site in Derby, Burnham said: "We've had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they're some kind of second-class citizens, and it's just not right.

"They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that's balanced between academic and technical."

The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet" - but declined to put a target date on his ambition.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

"It's hard to put a firm date on the moment when you can say there are fewer than now."

However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said while there was a "broad consensus" on improving vocational education, it was "not a big bold announcement".

She told BBC Breakfast: "What's going on there is a drastic shortage of jobs because Labour's policies over the last couple of years have killed job opportunities for young people. This announcement will not solve that."

News.title: People trapped inside Japan shopping centre after earthquake
News.content:
Several people are trapped inside a shopping centre after a strong earthquake hit south-west Japan, officials say.

Some local media reports that there was an explosion at the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, following the magnitude 7.1 earthquake.

The quake hit inland on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT), with more than 150,000 people being told to move to evacuation shelters. There was a brief tsunami warning that was lifted within the hour.

Emergency services said "many people" were trapped inside the Aeon Mall in the Kumamoto region.

In the town of Kashima, "a shopping complex's second floor collapsed, leaving many people trapped inside," the fire department said in a statement.

Japan is one of the world's most earthquake-prone countries, experiencing about 1,500 quakes a year.

The meteorological agency has warned of strong aftershocks given the shallow epicentre - 10km (six miles). Footage aired by national broadcaster NHK shows cracked roads and bridges and several buildings on fire.

"We are still assessing the extent of injuries and property damage, but I have been informed that there have already been several injuries," Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Tuesday.

About 10 of the injured were in an elderly care home and at least 50 people are being treated in hospital, NHK reported.

Train services have been suspended and electricity has been cut off for thousands of homes.

Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said first responders had been deployed, including Japan's self-defence force, fire services and coast guard.

"We urge residents in areas where the shaking was particularly severe to pay close attention to evacuation information issued by local authorities via radio, television and the internet, and to act calmly," he said.

News.title: Fourth heatwave grips parts of UK with 35C forecast
News.content:
A fourth heatwave of the year is now under way for parts of the UK, with temperatures expected to climb into the mid-30s Celsius later this week.

This latest spell of heatwave threshold-level temperatures is expected to peak on Wednesday in the south-east and east of England.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned the rising temperatures could increase health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.

It has issued amber heat health alerts, external for much of eastern England that come into force on Wednesday.

News.title: Zelensky to press Trump on air defences while in Washington
News.content:
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky is due to hold important talks with US President Donald Trump at the White House, where he is hoping to firm up commitments to bolstering Kyiv's anti-ballistic missile defences.

Zelensky has arrived in the US at a significant stage in Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine, with Moscow's mayor saying the capital was targeted by 390 drones in a matter of hours overnight.

The Ukrainian leader is expected to press Trump over support he gave earlier this month for Kyiv to be given a licence to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

Russia has escalated deadly ballistic missile attacks on Ukraine's capital recently, and Zelensky has said interceptors are urgently needed.

Patriot missiles have been at the top of Zelensky's wish-list for some time, but after the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, these US air defence interceptors are in very short supply.

Promising a licence is one thing, but co-producing the highly sophisticated PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors on Ukrainian soil is another, because it involves a lengthy political, legal and technical process.

A delegation from US manufacturer Raytheon visited Kyiv last week and Zelensky said the defence firm had expressed "readiness to take our partnership to an even higher level".

News.title: Naga Munchetty to leave BBC Breakfast after 17 years
News.content:
Munchetty is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about Â£360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.

She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.

In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.

She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.

In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.

However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.

In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.

In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct.

That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.

The BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously.

Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.

News.title: Badenoch calls for emergency legislation to stop early release scheme
News.content:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham to bring in emergency legislation in order to stop the early release of hundreds of prisoners.

Burnham announced last week that he was pausing the scheme, which would have seen about 700 prisoners freed in the first phase in September, following a backlash from survivors and victims.

But the Conservatives say the government's review will not stop offenders being released.

The scheme was part of a bid to stop unprecedented overcrowding, which Labour says was caused by Conservative governments failing to build new prisons.

A Labour spokesperson said: "It's this government that is fixing the Tories' mess."

On Tuesday, Burnham said: "It is a challenging situation and we shouldn't actually be in this position as a country, but we have to deal with the reality of where we are.

"But I will do anything I can to minimise risk to the public and that is why I am looking again and why I have put the release plan for September on hold and we'll make further statements on this in due course."

Early release was used by the Conservative government, external in 2023 because of prison overcrowding, first for 18 and then 70 days, and 10,000 prisoners had been released early by June 2024 - before Labour came to power.

When Sir Keir Starmer entered Downing Street in July 2024, there were fewer than 100 spare prison places across the adult male estate, which is what prompted the Sentencing Act to release another 6,000 prisoners early from September.

While the act already excludes some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences, the eligibility for early release is based on the length of fixed sentence, external, rather than the type of offence.

That means some criminals convicted of serious sexual and violent offences who have a fixed release date will leave prison earlier than they had expected - although subject to monitoring and risk of recall to prison.

Badenoch is calling on Burnham to fast-track legislation to keep serious offenders behind bars.

Speaking at a press conference alongside victims who could be impacted by the changes, the Conservative leader said: "It's quite clear that the prime minister sees that this is a problem, but I don't think he knows what to do about it."

She said she was concerned the pause would be "yet another thing where there will be warm words and nothing happens".

Without emergency legislation, Badenoch says dangerous offenders will start to be released the day after MPs return to Parliament after the summer recess on Tuesday 1 September.

She is calling on Burnham to revoke legislation coming into effect on 2 September and if necessary recall Parliament to ensure the worst violent and sexual offenders are exempted from early release.

Asked if the problem of prison overcrowding was a failing of the last Conservative government, she said the "crisis" had been "long time coming".

"We did something, it wasn't enough, I'm sorry about that," she said, adding: "I can't fix the past, what I can do is come up with solutions."

She said that to solve the problem of prison overcrowding in the long-run, the public needed to accept that some prisons would have to be built in their communities.

She also urged the government to consider renting prison places overseas.

Successive UK governments have explored the idea of sending prisoners to Estonia, however in 2025 the BBC was told that Conservative and Labour ministers had decided the plans would be too expensive.

Earlier this month, the Conservative front bench sought to put pressure on the government to rethink the earlier release plans, saying that it would mean some rapists would leave prison sooner than expected.

The government stood by the plan, saying it was a political choice to manage offenders on strict conditions in the community, rather than see the collapse of the system, leaving sex offenders and others to act with impunity.

Burnham's decision to pause the scheme came after criticism from the family of Thames Valley Police officer Andrew Harper, who was killed in Berkshire in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road by three teenagers.

Two of the killers of PC Harper, who were both sentenced to 13 years in prison, would have benefited from the scheme from June 2027, when the longest fixed sentences would have been added.

PC Harper's widow Lissie called the plans "deplorable" and said politicians were "making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences" for the families of victims.

Defending the review of the Sentencing Act that has been announced by Burnham, a Labour Party spokesperson said: "The Conservatives have some nerve.

"During their 14 years in office, they shut 23 prisons, created just 482 jail places, and granted early release to 10,000 prisoners - leaving the criminal justice system teetering on verge of collapse.

"It's this government that is fixing the Tories' mess. We have already delivered over 3,000 prison places and we're investing billions to deliver thousands more."

Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson Jess Brown-Fuller MP said: "The reality is that in a properly functioning justice system, no victim or loved ones should ever be told that their perpetrator is being released earlier than expected.

"Unfortunately, the Conservatives left our prisons on the brink of collapse, creating a capacity crisis that required emergency action to keep the system functioning and the public safe.

"Now that the government claims to have increased prison capacity, there is a clear opportunity for Burnham to correct some of the mistakes made by his predecessors with this scheme."

Reform UK's Home Affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said the "disastrous" policy had been introduced by the Tories, and Badenoch had in 2024 supported efforts to expand it.

"It's clear that only one party has consistently opposed early release and proposed strong law and order reforms to ensure hardened criminals are locked up for the full duration of their sentences," Yusuf said in a statement.

"Only Reform UK will fix lawless Britain," the party's Home Affairs spokesperson added.

News.title: 'I just found all the classified stuff downstairs,' Biden tells ghostwriter in recording
News.content:
Audio recordings that Joe Biden fought for years to keep private - in which he acknowledges possessing classified material after leaving office as US vice-president - have been released by Republicans in Congress.

The tapes contain interviews between Biden, now 83, and a ghostwriter working on his 2017 memoir, which was titled Promise Me, Dad.

"I just found all the classified stuff downstairs," Biden is heard saying at one point in the audio, recorded in February 2017, a month after he left the White House.

A US Department of Justice (DOJ) special counsel found in 2024 that Biden had improperly retained records but did not recommend charging him.

House Republicans and a conservative nonprofit, the Oversight Project, sued for the tapes as part of that probe into Biden's handling of the records.

Responding to the release of the tapes, Biden's spokesman TJ Ducklo criticised the direction of the justice department under President Donald Trump - saying the move was "just the latest example of this Administration weaponizing the DOJ for political retribution".

"It's wrong, and while President Biden disagrees with today's decision, he also respects the courts and the vital role an independent judiciary plays in a healthy democracy," Ducklo added.

The audio was recorded during the drafting of the 2017 memoir that Biden penned with co-writer Mark Zwonitzer.

At one point in the more than two hours of tapes released on Monday, Biden tells the ghostwriter: "The next thing I have here is, um, this is classified."

In an October 2016 recording, he tells Zwonitzer: "I have extensive notes over this period of timeâ¦ They [the White House] didn't know I have this."

At the time, Biden was still serving as vice-president to Barack Obama.

During Biden's tenure as president from 2021-25, the justice department declined to release the audio tapes.

In May, his personal lawyers sued the justice department in an effort to keep the tapes private, but after legal defeats they dropped their lawsuit.

The recordings contain significant redactions, which Republicans on the House Oversight Committee say "are intended to cover [Biden's] disclosure of classified information".

The recordings and transcripts were obtained by Special Counsel Robert Hur during his investigation in 2024 into Biden's handling of classified documents.

Explaining his decision not recommend charges, Hur said he had concerns that a jury would take Biden's side and view him as "a sympathetic, well-meaning, elderly man with a poor memory".

Trump was charged with illegally retaining the documents at his home in Florida, but the charges were dropped after he returned to the White House.

News.title: Devastating European wildfires in maps - and how they're being tackled
News.content:
Wildfires are tearing through France and Spain, forcing more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.

France has seen its worst fires in two decades, while officials in the Spanish capital Madrid say they are the worst the region has ever experienced.

It follows a sweltering summer of heatwaves across Europe that have seen temperatures soar above 40C (104F) in many places.

Separate wildfires in the regions outside Madrid have together burned about 297 sq miles (770 sq km), authorities estimate - an area larger than the city itself.

News.title: Unsolved Suzy Lamplugh case 'haunts' detectives
News.content:
Police officers investigating the disappearance of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh in west London say they remain "haunted" by the case, four decades after she went missing.

Lamplugh, 25, vanished after leaving her Fulham office to meet a client on the afternoon of 28 July 1986. She never returned and her body has never been found.

As the Metropolitan Police investigation is due to be mothballed next year, cold case detectives say they are troubled by the continuing mystery.

To mark the 40th anniversary of her disappearance, the Lamplugh family has released previously unseen photographs featuring her siblings Lizzie, Tamsin and Richard and her parents Paul and Diana.

In releasing the intimate family images, her siblings described her as "a truly beautiful person inside and out".

News.title: Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
News.content:
The morning-after pill, known as emergency contraception, external, is medication designed to prevent unwanted pregnancies. It usually has to be taken within three to five days of having unprotected sex. The sooner it is taken, the more effective it is.

It works by delaying or preventing the release of an egg, but will only prevent pregnancy if ovulation has not already happened.

Alternatively, women can visit a doctor or nurse to have a coil or intrauterine device (IUD) fitted to prevent pregnancy at any time during their menstrual cycle. To be effective, it needs to be fitted within 120 hours or five days of unprotected sex.

The government said making the morning-after pill available free from pharmacies would end the "unfair" barriers and postcode lottery some women faced - with access varying dramatically depending on where they live.

Under the scheme, women can visit their local pharmacy and have a confidential consultation with a pharmacist or trained pharmacy technician, before receiving the medication on the same day.

Prior to this, women had to book an appointment with their GP, sexual health clinic or pharmacy to get the morning-after pill. Women could also access it privately, as they still can now.

In 2024/25, there were around 150,000 NHS prescriptions for the morning-after pill - far fewer than under the new service.

Dr Sue Mann, NHS National Clinical Director for Women's Health, said the pharmacy service was a "major step forward for women's health", with "no appointment, no waiting and no judgement".

"This service is already making a real impact, particularly for women living in more deprived communities, by making contraception easier to access closer to home," she added.

Women can check online, external to find their nearest participating pharmacy. All pharmacists and pharmacy technicians delivering the service have received specialist training to provide emergency contraception and wider contraceptive care.

News.title: Love Island UK crowns winners of twist-filled series
News.content:
This article contains spoilers for the Love Island final.

Julia Majchrzak and Lorenzo Alessi have been crowned the winners of Love Island UK 2026.

The pair beat runners-up Jasmine Muller and Kavan Murphy, and Angelista Gunda and Simba Kudyiwa, who came in third, to take home the Â£50,000 prize.

A shocked Julia thanked all those who had voted for them, saying: "I just didn't think coming into Casa [Amor] I'd be stood here."

When host Maya Jama asked what they would spend the money on, Julia revealed she wanted Lorenzo, who appeared too stunned to speak, to move in with her after leaving the villa.

Talking to Maya ahead of the reveal during the live final, 28-year-old Lorenzo said he had "never met someone who feels so well matched to me" when reflecting on his relationship with Julia.

Business owner Lorenzo, who entered the villa on day one, said he felt like he "manifested" meeting Julia, 26, in Casa Amor, the alternate villa where relationships are tested by new arrivals.

Julia said she felt an "instant spark" when meeting Lorenzo and described their relationship as "seriously unserious".

News.title: Second home owners 'feel unwelcome' while locals struggle to buy
News.content:
Rhodri Lewis is desperate to buy a house in his home county of Pembrokeshire, an area in which the Welsh government estimated 6.5%, external of all properties were second homes in 2023-24.

"When I did have a look around, there was no chance I was going to be able to afford a house," the 23-year-old said.

"So, yeah, I had to move back in with mum and dad, unfortunately."

Rhodri is a Welsh speaker and like many other people, he said he worries that a lack of affordable housing for local people can affect the language.

"Tourism is fantastic for us for three months of the year in the summer," he said.

"But then the other eight, nine months, where a lot of the second homes, for example, don't have people in them, it just kills the community for the rest of the year."

Rhodri is planning to travel in the near future and hopes he'll be able to afford his first home upon his return.

Carol Peet, who sells properties in Pembrokeshire, said she believed in some areas there are two housing markets: one for locals and one for second homes.

"The obvious answer to it, I think, which I've been selling for the last 25 years is to stop houses under the average price of a property in this area, which at the moment is about Â£250,000, being sold as second homes," she said.

"Those are the properties that young local families can afford, not the million-pound houses that second homers buy."

She added that a number of "chocolate box pretty cottages" are great for holidays but are "totally impractical" for full-time living as "they're cold, damp and dark in the winter".

She said that while second homes were "absolutely vital" to her local economy in Narberth, she understood the need for affordable housing for local people.

News.title: 'We lost all of our morning trade' - businesses fearful after more break-ins
News.content:
Pride weekend is one of the busiest of the year for many city centre businesses, but for one chip shop owner Saturday morning was spent filing police reports after his shop became the latest to be targeted in Belfast.

Gareth McKinstry, who owns Simply Fish & Chips, said it was a costly incident.

Last week another cafÃ© owner warned the situation was at a "tipping point" after his premises were targeted.

Since then, three more city centre businesses have been broken into and money stolen, including McKinstry's restaurant on Oxford Street.

"Saturday was Pride day and it was meant to be one of our busiest days of the year and we lost all of our morning trade because we couldn't open the shop until the police had finished with their investigation," McKinstry said.

The break-in happened at about 02:00 BST on Saturday.

Belfast is preparing to welcome hundreds of thousands of visitors to the city for the all-Ireland music and dance festival, Fleadh Cheoil na hÃireann, which begins on Sunday.

McKinstry said he now needed to work to get the shop ready for the festival.

"I need to get repairs for the window. It's not what we needed and it's not what anybody in Belfast needs, but it seems to be becoming a more common thing happening at the moment," he said.

News.title: How afraid should we be of Scotland's jellyfish?
News.content:
When scuba diver and underwater photographer Ross McLaren encountered a jellyfish for the first time, he said all he felt was "sheer terror".

"I was diving in the Clyde and one of the instructors had to pull me out of the way of the tentacles as it was wafting above me," he said.

McLaren ended up with a sting across his upper lip but said it did not stop him from wanting to dive.

Many people are scared of jellyfish due to the fear of painful stings and the creature's unpredictable nature in the water.

News.title: Reform UK reports Zack Polanski to police over guillotine T-shirt post
News.content:
Reform UK have reported Green Party leader Zack Polanski to the police, after he shared an Instagram post including a photo of a man wearing a top featuring the name "Nigel" alongside an image of a guillotine.

One of several images showed a man in a black t-shirt with a large guillotine below the words "We're only making plans for Nigel".

Sharing a screenshot on X, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski."

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Once this image was brought to [Zack's] attention he immediately unshared the post. He unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message."

Polanski had shared the photo with his 713,000 followers in a post containing several pictures of a Green Party event on Sunday, having accepted a request to collaborate with another account.

In a post on X, the Metropolitan Police said: "We received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media. We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting enquiries into the matter."

The words "We're only making plans for Nigel" are the same as the lyrics of a 1979 song by band XTC, external.

The Green Party spokesperson said: "Zack condemns the image on the T-shirt. He was tagged in a post with 20 images and clicked accept without realising there was more to it than he had seen.

"The T-shirt is clearly in poor taste, especially at a time of heightened fears for the security of public figures, having experienced multiple threats himself.

"He and the Green Party call on everyone involved in public discourse to show kindness and not encourage more division."

The BBC understands Polanski has not been contacted by police.

Reform UK say Polanski has not been in touch with Farage to privately apologise for sharing the post. The Greens have been approached for comment in relation to this.

News.title: Very strong tide led to West Mersea drownings, relative says
News.content:
A mother and daughter who drowned off the Essex coast were swept out to sea by a "very strong" tide, a relative has said.

Shahin Ahmed said six members of his family were paddling at West Mersea beach when they were knocked off their feet on Wednesday afternoon.

Shelina Rahman, 41, and 15-year-old Sameeha, died in the tragedy, while Ahmed's seven-year-old son Musa was airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.

Ahmed said his son, who is from east London, remained on a life support machine at a hospital in London.

Three others were also taken to another hospital by ambulance after the incident. Ahmed said 12 of them were visiting West Mersea that day.

"This was 20 minutes before we were going to go home. The whole day, alhamdulillah (praise be to God), was really nice," Ahmed told Bangladeshi newspaper Surma News.
