The “Burnham bounce” has seen Labour take a lead in three national polls – days before the new prime minister is set to crush Reform UK in the first major test of his premiership.

A Survation poll published on Tuesday morning put Labour top with 26 per cent, up one point, with Nigel Farage’s party trailing with 24 per cent, down two points.

It followed More in Common released on Monday which put Labour ahead with 28 per cent compared to Reform’s 24 per cent. A YouGov poll gave both parties 22 per cent on Monday.

The findings show Reform’s dominance of polling – leading in more than 300 consecutive surveys since April 2025 – has come to a shattering end as Mr Farage’s hopes of becoming prime minister appear to be evaporating after Labour’s change of leader.

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham during a visit to Alstom Transport in Derby to unveil a change to the education system (Temilade Adelaja/PA) ( PA Wire )

In another blow for Reform, Labour are eyeing a landslide victory in the Manchester mayor by-election, a contest which was called after Mr Burnham resigned from that position to pave a return to Westminster.

According to polling from More in Common, Labour’s candidate Bev Craig would secure 39 per cent of the vote on Thursday, while Reform expected to gain around 19 per cent. The Greens are currently in third place with 14 per cent, with the Tories on 12 per cent.

In the subsequent run-off, Labour would get around two thirds of the votes against Reform, according to the poll.

When the contest began, Reform were the narrow favourites after the local elections showed they had the highest level of support in Greater Manchester.

Local election results on 7 May in the region gave Reform 30.8 per cent, Labour 23.6 per cent, the Greens 19 per cent and Conservatives 10.4 per cent.

Leading polling expert Lord Hayward told The Independent that the surveys have “changed the discourse of British politics.”

He said: “We are no longer talking about Reform becoming the government – in fact, there is an open question over whether they are the natural party of the right.”

open image in gallery Nigel Farage’s dreams of becoming PM are evaporating ( PA )

He pointed out that the Tories are in third place in the polls but are now closing the gap on Reform, with Survation putting Kemi Badenoch’s party up two points to 21 per cent.

Lord Hayward added: “There is no doubt there is a Burnham bounce and it has happened quicker than most of us expected.

“Part of it is Andy Burnham himself, his policies and communication and part of it is that Keir Starmer is no longer there.

“That has coincided with a marked decline in support for Reform. They have real problems.”

The peer also noted that Mr Burnham “is using August very well, just as Nigel Farage did last year” with a series of announcements, social media videos and putting Labour on the front foot.

“In contrast, Reform don’t seem to be able to do anything that can halt their decline,” he added.

Mr Farage is currently bogged down in a by-election in Clacton after resigning his seat to trigger a vote. An investigation into a £5 million donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harbourne is hanging over his head, as well as another into gifts and support he received from convicted money launderer George Cottrell.

None of the major parties are contesting what Ms Badenoch described as “a fake by-election”, leaving 34 fringe opponents – most notably the comedic candidate Count Binface.

But a Reform spokesman insisted that the party is “calm” about the turn in polling.

He said: “We expected Labour to go above us, we are calm about it. Let’s see where everyone is by December.”

In a note on how things can change, the spokesman added: “Two years ago Keir Starmer was flying high in the polls, there were comment pieces talking about him being a sex symbol and the ‘grown ups were back in charge’.”

Meanwhile, Mr Burnham said he would not get “carried away” but was pleased to have “connected with people” after a poll gave Labour its first lead for more than a year.

The prime minister told reporters on a visit to Portsmouth: “I wouldn’t get carried away by any poll. I’m pleased to have made a start where hopefully I’ve connected with people.

“And I am talking a lot about Britain believing again and getting its hope back, and I’m not going to apologise for that. I think we should have a bit more of a spring in our step.”

He added that he would “address some of those big issues this week”, including youth unemployment, social care and housing.

Eurostar has announced the launch of a new direct route between the UK and Belgium from December.

From 14 December, rail travellers will be able to book direct journeys from London St Pancras to Antwerp-Centraal.

Up to four trains a day, which already run between London and Amsterdam, will introduce the direct connection with existing stops at Lille-Europe, Brussels-Midi, Rotterdam-Centraal and Amsterdam-Centraal.

However, the route will only be direct on the outward leg from London.

According to Eurostar, there are no current plans to introduce a direct return service from Antwerp to London as “this would require dedicated UK border and customs facilities at Antwerp-Centraal”.

Customers can instead book a combined SNCB and Eurostar ticket through the Channel Tunnel operator connecting via Brussels-Midi, where UK border and security checks take place.

Eurostar said: “Adding Antwerp as a direct stop on our London-Amsterdam services will make journeys to the city quicker and more convenient, providing customers with a more comfortable city centre to city centre travel experience.”

The international high-speed train service is also preparing for unprecedented heat across Europe with a new fleet of trains designed to withstand temperatures of up to 55C.

Following intense heatwaves, including a record-breaking high of 37.7C in the UK in June, Eurostar has said it will upgrade its new fleet with air conditioning capable of operating at 55C.

The Channel Tunnel rail operator upgraded its order with French manufacturer Alstom earlier this month to “be prepared for the future”.

Last year, Eurostar announced a €2bn (£1.7bn) investment in up to 50 new double-decker all-electric Celestia trains.

It said: “We’ve confirmed an order for 30 trains, with an option for a further 20, marking a significant step in our growth journey to 30 million annual passengers.”

News.title: ‘Evil’ funeral director treated bodies ‘like a piece of meat’ as families left distraught
News.content:

A funeral director who kept 35 decomposing bodies at a site in Hull and gave families the wrong ashes had treated a dead pensioner “like a piece of meat”, a court has heard.

Robert Bush, 48, was found with half a tonne of ashes, with some families forced to wait seven weeks for DNA tests to identify their loved ones.

One woman described Bush as “pure evil” after he gave her the wrong ashes of her brother Paul Hemingway, which her children then had made into jewellery.

Terry White’s daughter Angela Scottow also said that she was handed the wrong ashes, and that her family had lit candles around them on his birthday to celebrate his life.

“Dad was such a lovely man and Rob Bush treated him like a piece of meat,” she said. “I feel only anger, hatred and disgust for the man that I trusted to treat my dad with dignity and respect.”

open image in gallery Robert Bush pictured arriving at Hull Crown Court for his five-day sentencing ( AFP/Getty )

She added: “He has absolutely broken me. How will I trust anyone again?”

The court heard the body of 88-year-old Peter Brown was found at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors more than a month after his death with his hearing aids still in place, while 80-year-old Jim Porter’s body was found with hospital identification bands still on his wrists.

The grandson of Susan Stone, 77, whose body was also found at Legacy, said that his grandfather was “destroyed” by the discovery.

Hull Crown Court heard over 12 years, Bush breached the trust placed in him by grieving families “on an almost industrial scale”, by keeping bodies for months after they should have been cremated, giving out the wrong ashes, taking money for funeral plans without making any of the arrangements and stealing charity donations collected at services.

open image in gallery Bush had kept 35 bodies at his funeral home in Hull ( PA )

One woman said she feels she has let her mother down after her ashes “can’t be located anywhere”.

In a victim personal statement, Claire Edwards said: “I am so angry that I placed trust in Bush from the start, and that he has let us down as a family, and I feel that I personally have let my mum down.

“I feel guilty about what happened with my mum’s funeral arrangements and that I am unable to place my mum’s ashes with my late dad’s ashes – which were hers/our wishes.”

His crimes were discovered by chance, when he was on holiday in Arizona and contacted Gary Pickering and Steve Emmerson, directors of Evergreen Funeral Directors, asking them to assist with a body recovery while he was away.

Patrick Moore – a casual worker for Legacy – helped the two men collect the body from the care home, but said Bush had told him “not to bring anyone back to Legacy or help put a body into the fridge area”.

After becoming suspicious that operations at Legacy were not as they should be, the two men persuaded Mr Moore to let them into Legacy’s site on Hessle Road, which was described as a “horror scene”.

open image in gallery The bodies were discovered by chance while Bush was on holiday in Arizona ( PA )

They flagged down a passing police car after discovering bodies “uncovered and in varying states of decomposition”, with the funeral home described as “dirty and unkempt” and a human foetus discovered in a brown bag.

Robert Bush committed fraud concerning the ashes of 57 people between 2017 and 2024, Hull Crown Court has heard.

The total value of this fraud is around £86,868 with 46 victims identified where ashes have been wrongly returned to families, and an additional 11 families where no ashes have ever been returned, prosecutor Chris Paxton KC said.

He added that the “lack of book keeping” by Bush was “quite profound”, making it “very difficult to follow” the number of funerals overseen by the him during this time.

Bush has admitted 67 offences, including preventing a lawful and decent burial, fraudulent trading, fraud by false representation and theft from well-known charities.

This includes four “foetus allegations” of fraud where he presented ashes to women, falsely saying they were “the remains of their unborn”.

The BBC has announced that Naga Munchetty will be leaving BBC Breakfast after 17 years on the show.

Munchetty, who first joined BBC Breakfast as a stand-in presenter back in 2009, will be heading to BBC Radio 5 Live, where she will present its flagship morning programme from January 2027. The move follows a series of personnel and schedule changes on the show, with weekend host Rachel Burden announcing earlier this month that she would also be leaving the series.

In a statement, Munchetty said that she’s “thrilled” to be joining 5 Live Breakfast. “Live news, great conversations and connecting with audiences are what I love most about broadcasting, and 5 Live does all of that brilliantly,” she said.

“It has been a privilege to be part of the BBC Breakfast TV team for the past 17 years, working alongside an incredibly talented and hard-working group of journalists who are not only outstanding colleagues but also great friends.

“Presenting a flagship programme on 5 Live is an opportunity that was simply too good to pass up. It will take a huge amount of work and require 100% of my focus and energy, and I'm really looking forward to throwing myself into the role.”

Having presented the station’s weekday mid-morning programme since 2021, Munchetty added that she’s “excited to build” on her existing relationship with listeners. “Between now and January, I’ll continue presenting the two programmes I love,” she said. “I’m sure there will be plenty of news to cover, and it will very much be business as usual.”

open image in gallery Munchetty will be taking over the 5Live Breakfast slot ( BBC )

As for the current hosts of 5Live Breakfast, Rick Edwards and Burden announced on Tuesday (28 July) that they would be stepping down from the show in December. Instead, Burden will host the weekday mid-morning programme, while Edwards continues to present Fighting Talk, which airs on the station on Saturday mornings.

“After 15 years hosting 5 Live Breakfast, I’ve decided it’s time for a change – and I’m really excited about launching my new show on the station,” Burden said. “It’s been an absolute joy and privilege to be part of our listeners’ mornings for all these years. We have been through life-changing events together – from the pandemic to huge political moments, and great sporting journeys.

“They are my extended family, and we’ll carry on doing what we do best – telling stories, sharing experiences and working out the world together. Just this time, on a little bit more sleep.”

open image in gallery Rick Edwards and Rachel Burden are leaving Radio 5 Live’s Breakfast show ( 5 Live/BBC )

Edwards added that his five years on the show look “inconsequential” next to Burden’s 15.

“I’ll really miss our wonderful audience, I’ll miss the fantastic team, I’ll miss regularly eating cake before dawn, but most of all I’ll miss Rach – a colleague who has become a friend, and also a mentor, because she’s so much older than me,” he added.

“Two things I am of course looking forward to are not waking up at 3.45am, and vaping without fear of violent recrimination.”

Munchetty is set to broadcast live from Salford for three days a week, while the remaining two will be from London. She’ll also be joined by a new co-host on 5 Live Breakfast, who will be announced later in the year.

A Louisiana man who spent nearly three decades on death row walked free Wednesday after courts concluded his murder conviction relied on discredited bite-mark evidence that judges described as "junk science."

Jimmie "Chris" Duncan was released on a $150,000 bond after his 1998 first-degree murder conviction was overturned. He had been convicted of raping and murdering 23-month-old Haley Oliveaux, the daughter of his then-girlfriend, Allison Layton Statham.

Fourth Judicial District Judge Alvin Sharp vacated the conviction in April after hearing expert testimony that the forensic evidence used to convict Duncan was "not scientifically defensible" and that the toddler's death appeared consistent with an accidental drowning. Last month, the Louisiana Supreme Court ruled that "no rational juror" would convict Duncan based on the scientific evidence presented at his original trial.

open image in gallery This 2017 photo provided by the Mwalimu Center for Justice shows Jimmie Duncan with family friend at the Louisiana State Penitentiary in the community of Angola ( Mwalimu Center for Justice )

"The presumption is not great that he is guilty," Sharp wrote in granting Duncan bail, citing the new forensic evidence and Duncan's lack of any prior criminal history.

Duncan's attorneys called the ruling a major step toward clearing his name, saying the court had found "clear and convincing evidence" pointing to his factual innocence.

The case has become one of the nation's highest-profile examples of convictions built on bite-mark analysis, a once-common forensic technique that has since been widely discredited. An Associated Press review in 2013 identified at least two dozen wrongful convictions or criminal charges since 2000 that relied on bite-mark evidence.

open image in gallery Duncan was held here at the Louisiana State Penitentiary in Angola, Louisiana ( AFP/Getty )

Prosecutors' case centered on testimony from forensic dentist Michael West and pathologist Steven Hayne, whose work has since been linked to multiple wrongful convictions. Duncan's legal team argued the pair relied on flawed methods that modern forensic science has rejected.

Court filings from Duncan's attorneys allege a videotaped examination showed West pressing a mold of Duncan's teeth into the child's body before concluding the marks matched his bite. A state expert who later testified at trial was unaware of how the marks had been created, according to the defense.

Hayne has since died. West has acknowledged that DNA testing has largely made bite-mark analysis obsolete but has defended his work in cases that were later overturned.

open image in gallery Duncan's release from Death Row comes months after Gov. Jeff Landry, shown here, pushed for the use of nitrogen gas in state executions ( Getty )

During Duncan's bail hearing, Haley's mother delivered some of the most emotional testimony in the case, telling the judge she no longer believes Duncan killed her daughter.

Instead, Allison Layton Statham said Haley, who had a history of seizures, accidentally drowned in the bathtub.

"Haley died because she was sick," Statham testified, according to court records.

She said prosecutors never informed her of evidence that could have cleared Duncan and accused investigators and forensic experts of creating a false narrative that devastated both families.

open image in gallery According to the Death Penalty Information Center, more than 200 death row inmates have been exonerated nationwide since 1973, including 12 in Louisiana. The state's last death row exoneration came in 2016 ( AP2009 )

"The horror story that they put out and desecrated my baby's memory makes me infuriated," she told the court. "I was not informed of anything that would have exonerated Mr. Duncan at all. Had I been then, things would have turned out a lot different for Mr. Duncan and all of our families."

Innocence Project attorney M. Chris Fabricant told the court that "bite mark evidence is junk science," arguing there is no more prejudicial form of unreliable forensic evidence.

The case also highlights Louisiana's long history of wrongful convictions. According to the Death Penalty Information Center, more than 200 death row inmates have been exonerated nationwide since 1973, including 12 in Louisiana. The state's last death row exoneration came in 2016.

open image in gallery Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill opposed Duncan's release ( Getty )

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill opposed Duncan's release, arguing he should remain behind bars while the state Supreme Court reviews prosecutors' effort to reinstate the conviction. The high court, however, allowed the district judge to decide whether Duncan could be released on bail.

Prosecutors continue to seek reinstatement of Duncan's conviction and are still pursuing the death penalty. The Ouachita Parish District Attorney's Office has declined to comment because the appeal remains pending before the Louisiana Supreme Court.

Duncan, who had been one of 55 inmates on Louisiana's death row at the Louisiana State Penitentiary at Angola, plans to live with relatives in central Louisiana while the legal battle over his case continues. His attorneys described him as a model prisoner who spent years helping fellow death row inmates earn their GEDs and said he has strong community support as he continues his fight for full exoneration.

A fourth live-action Paddington film is in development with A-list talent, Canal+ CEO Maxime Saada confirmed on Tuesday, adding fresh momentum to one of StudioCanal's biggest international franchises.

The pay-TV provider will also be the first to bring Paddington 4 to French small screens, just six months after its theatrical release. This follows their renewed agreement with French cinema organisations until 2032, committing investments for early access to new releases.

The group did not disclose the film's release date or distribution plans. Canal+ will invest about €1 billion ($1.2 billion) in French and European ​cinema ⁠over five years starting ‌from 2028. In return, it is granted privileged access to new theatrical releases under France's media laws, both for ‌its own films and acquired content — an ‌advantage as global streaming services compete for subscribers.

open image in gallery The previous Paddington movies were released in 2014, 2017 and 2024 and proved to be a huge success at the box office. ( PA )

"When we buy and we have deals with Universal, Warner, Paramount ... all of these ⁠movies are available on the Canal+ platform in France six months after release. When Netflix has a deal with Universal, they have to wait until 15 months to broadcast the movie (in France)," Saada told Reuters.

To secure the right to early releases, Canal+ is required to invest about €140 million a year, Saada said. "So we committed to spending an extra €50 million a year, approximately." The investment is ‌only one part of ⁠the group's much larger content budget. Canal+ spent €2.25 billion ⁠in content costs in the first half of 2026 alone, across films, ‌television and ​sport in its international markets. France generated €1.77 ‌billion of its first-half revenue, ​making it Canal+'s biggest individual market.

Earlier this year, Actor Hugh Bonneville indicated he is unlikely to return to the Paddington film franchise.

The 62-year-old, who plays Mr Brown in the children’s films, suggested the series would continue without him as its focus remains on the bear.

Asked about a potential return to Paddington, he told Saga Magazine: "I don’t think so. I really don’t. I’ve loved it, but I’m getting on a bit. It’s a younger man’s job, but you can get other actors in and it will work just as well, because it’s all about the bear."

Armando Iannucci, the Oscar-nominated screenwriter behind the sweary, satirical classic The Thick Of It, has also been revealed as the writer for Paddington 4.

open image in gallery Actor Hugh Bonneville has revealed he will not return to the Paddington film franchise. ( PA Wire )

The Scottish writer – who also penned Veep, The Death of Stalin and the admittedly more niche 2006 series Time Trumpet – has reportedly joined as one half of the writing team who will mastermind the Peruvian bear’s next adventure.

According to Variety, Iannucci will reunite with frequent collaborator Simon Blackwell for the project, which was announced at ComicCon earlier this year.

Paddington, first published on October 13 1958, has seen a number of adaptations over the years, including a BBC TV version in 1976, voiced by the late Sir Michael Hordern.

The movies, featuring Ben Whishaw as the voice of Paddington, produced by StudioCanal, were released in 2014, 2017 and 2024 and proved to be a huge success at the box office.

Paddington The Musical is currently playing in London’s West End at the Savoy Theatre.

The stage show features original music by McFly’s Tom Fletcher. "It’s an honour to be entrusted to bring the story of Paddington to life on stage with the very best of creative collaborators in (playwright) Jessica (Swale), (theatre director) Luke (Sheppard), and our producers Sonia (Friedman) and Eliza (Lumley),” Fletcher said.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
Global tech stocks have plunged after China achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom.

Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight in a worldwide sell-off of semiconductor companies, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

The downturn was triggered by reports that a Chinese state-owned company had begun mass-producing machinery critical to the manufacture of advanced microchips used for AI.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of so-called deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to tech publication The Information. These machines, until recently dominated by Western companies, can be as big as a double-decker bus and use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Leading Chinese chipmakers are expected to receive the first deliveries of the machines later this year.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on miniscule circuits invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers on to microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

News.title: Amazon has ended support for pre-2013 Kindles. What to do if you’re affected (and what to avoid)
News.content:
It seems like a lot of devices, but Amazon told Engadget that the move will affect around three per cent of current users. In theory, if you’re using a device that’s affected, then Amazon should already have notified you via email. If in doubt, however, the company has a support page with pictures and specifications of every Kindle ever released. If you’re still unsure, entering the model number into Google should reveal the exact version you’re using. This can typically be found on the back of devices.

For Kindle Fire tablets, the process is simpler. Open the Settings menu and select “Device Options”. You’ll find the model you’re using either under “Device Model” or “About Fire Tablet”.

Why did this happen?

Nobody expects electronic devices to be supported forever, but it’s disappointing that the Kindle’s most enthusiastic early adopters got cut off. Given the basic functionality of e-book reader technology, there doesn’t appear to be a technical reason behind the decision, making it appear like an anti-consumer move to push older customers towards the purchase of newer devices where existing Kindles would become an e-waste casualty.

When asked why these devices were losing support, we received a response defending the (admittedly impressive) longevity.

“These models have been supported for at least 14 years – some as long as 18 years – but technology has come a long way in that time, and these devices will no longer be supported moving forward,” an Amazon spokesperson said. “We are notifying those still actively using them and offering promotions to help with the transition to newer devices.”

At the initial time of writing, the promotions mentioned appeared to be 20 per cent off “select new Kindle devices” alongside a £15 eBook credit. While the latter was welcome, the highlighted discount is somewhat disappointing for a number of reasons. Firstly, according to the promotion’s terms and conditions, the “select” caveat excludes the most expensive model, the Kindle Scribe. It doesn’t apply to Fire devices for those tablet owners looking to replace like-for-like, either.

More importantly, the prices aren’t all that impressive considering happy owners of older Kindles weren’t budgeting for this purchase. Amazon frequently discounts its own-brand devices like Echo smart speakers and Fire tablets, and 20 per cent isn’t that unusual. Last year’s Black Friday sale saw discounts of over 30 per cent on the basic Kindle and Kindle Colorsoft, and the price-tracking site CamelCamelCamel shows that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition has been as low as £183 in the past – a 32 per cent discount on its current price of £269.

There was added time pressure, too. Amazon said the discount and credit offer was only valid until June 20, one month after support for the older Kindles ended.

Additionally, owners of the earliest UK Kindle will see that prices have gone up over the past decade. The £109 they paid in 2010 is some way off the £159.99 Kindle Paperwhite, even with a 20 per cent discount, let alone the £219.99 Kindle Colorsoft. That said, at £94.99, the basic Kindle 12th Generation remains a bargain for no-frills readers, with a 20 per cent discount taking it down to £75.99.

Possible upgrades

If you’re affected by this news, the silver lining is that while e-book technology moves relatively slowly, things have still advanced significantly in the past 14 years. Resolutions are higher; most are backlit for bedtime reading; there’s support for audiobooks; and storage has increased. There are also optional extras like colour screens, blue-light filters to prevent eye strain and waterproofing.

As outlined in our guide to the best Kindles, our pick for most people is the 12th Generation Kindle Paperwhite, which costs £159.99 with lockscreen ads or £169.99 without. The seven inch screen with warm lighting makes for a comfortable reading experience, and it’s waterproof for bathtime or poolside reading.

At £94.99 (or £104.99 without ads), the basic 11th Generation Kindle is a great budget pick, however. It’s slightly smaller at six inches, and like the Paperwhite, can hold around 8,000 e-books with support for audiobooks through Audible. It lacks the warm light and waterproofing, however, and its battery life is around half that of the Paperwhite — albeit still a generous six weeks of normal use.

The two remaining Kindles occupy specific niches. The Kindle Colorsoft has a colour screen, making it well suited to those who enjoy graphic novels. The Kindle Scribe, meanwhile, has a bundled stylus for note taking.

Can I still use my old Kindle?

Yes, Amazon said users would be able to “continue to read books already downloaded on these devices”. If you factory reset your older Kindle, however, or you deregister it, you won’t be able to use it anymore.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

Sports.title: Chelsea star abruptly leaves pre-season tour to seal transfer away from club
Sports.content:
FILIP JORGENSEN has left Chelsea’s pre-season tour as he looks to get a move away from the club over the line.

Xabi Alonso‘s side are currently in Australia as they kick off their preparations with a friendly.

But goalkeeper Jorgensen will no longer be with the side, after jetting back to the UK.



The Dane is pursuing a move away from Stamford Bridge, where he traded the No1 spot with Robert Sanchez last season.



He was given a string of chances to impress under Liam Rosenior after his arrival in January.

But things got ugly after his howler derailed his side at home against Paris Saint-Germain.

He then got injured in the wake of the result, requiring surgery on his groin.

It was reported then that the 24-year-old was keen on leaving the club when the summer window rolled around.

And now that has seemingly come to fruition, though his destination remains uncertain.

Jorgensen was absent from the squad kicking off the tour in a friendly with Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez injury update after Man Utd star’s World Cup final heartache as transfer plan revealed
Sports.content:
LISANDRO MARTINEZ has handed Manchester United a huge boost after edging closer to winning his battle to be fit for the start of the new season.

The defender, 28, was heartbroken when he was forced off with an injury during the first half of the World Cup final.



Martinez was then helpless as his Argentina team-mates crashed to a 1-0 defeat against Spain after extra-time.

And United were concerned they would be without the former Ajax man when their campaign gets underway against newly-promoted Hull on August 22.



But Martinez’s injury is not as bad as first feared after tests revealed he had suffered a muscle strain.

And the centre-back, who bagged a spot in the World Cup’s team of the tournament, should be back in time for the trip to the MKM Stadium.

United’s medical staff started piecing together a recovery plan as soon as Martinez went down clutching his thigh.

And recruitment chiefs also weighed up entering the transfer market for a replacement.

But positive news over Martinez’s lay-off has resulted in United deciding not to pursue a fresh option at the heart of the backline.

Old Trafford boss Michael Carrick, who was rewarded with a two-year deal after masterminding the Red Devils’ push for Champions League qualification last term, has been prioritising midfield additions.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He forked out a whopping £50million to tempt Andrey Santos away from Chelsea.

And the Brazilian was quickly followed through the door by Youri Tielemans.

The Belgian joined in a £35m deal after United triggered a bargain release clause written into his Aston Villa contract.

Karl Darlow has also been recruited as a back-up goalkeeper following his decision to snub fresh terms at Leeds.



Injuries limited Martinez to just 18 Premier League appearances last season.

And he was controversially sent off for pulling Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s hair during the loss to Leeds in April.

Sports.title: Teen who doesn’t even play for Chelsea scores their first goal just minutes into friendly vs Western Sydney Wanderers
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’s first goal of pre-season was scored by a TRIALIST who doesn’t even officially play for them yet.

Kazakhstan wonderkid Dastan Satpayev, 17, is not a registered Blues player until his birthday next month – but still bagged within seven minutes against Western Sydney Wanderers.



Satpayev was picked up by the Blues last year from Kazak side Kairat Almaty.

And the forward, wearing No36, made a blistering start when put through on goal at the Accor Stadium.



He surged through the middle of the pitch and smashed in a finish at the near post.

Baby-faced attacker Satpayev was sent through from deep by Cobham academy graduate Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.



A sheepish Satpayev, who played in the Champions League last season for European minnows Kairat, celebrated his goal with young defender Olutayo Subuloye.

Kavuma-McQueen, Reggie Walsh, and Liam Delap all joined him in a round of high fives.

Satpayev trained with Alonso at Chelsea’s pre-season camp prior to flying out to Australia.

He was named in the touring squad and became a big attraction for fans at their open training session in Sydney.



Satpayev was a huge draw for supporters with Kazakhstan flags in the crowd of 5,000 at the Allianz Stadium over the weekend.

Chelsea were aware of the fanfare he might get as a bright light of his country’s game.

They agreed to buy him for around £3.5million but did not need any special dispensation for him to feature.

His five year deal at Stamford Bridge will not kick into gear until he turns 18.

Chelsea simply needed permission from Kairat for him to play – as well as trial forms being signed and parental permission.



Satpayev scored 26 times in 58 appearances for the Kairat senior side and made his full international debut in March 2025.

He netted first goal against Belgium in November and now has a chance to prove what he can do.

Chelsea have not yet decided if he will stay at the club, go on loan, or play in the academy moving forward.

Alonso picked a team full of kids for his first game – although Chelsea did play two behind-closed-doors friendlies last week against EFL sides Crawley and Bromley.

Satpayev was joined by Cobham hopefuls Landon Emenalo, Reggie Watson, Subuloye, Walsh, and Kavuma-McQueen with star power left on the bench in the first half.

Sports.title: Chelsea files: Academy star, 16, leaves Xabi Alonso impressed and Robert Sanchez’s awkward pre-season reunion
Sports.content:
JET LAG has been a huge consideration as Chelsea embark on their mammoth tour of Australia and Asia.

Ahead of their flight to Sydney, via Sri Lanka, from London, the Blues sports science department pulled out all the stops to help players and staff survive the journey.



All of Chelsea‘s travelling party were provided with a masterplan to beat jet leg from the second they boarded their flight at London Gatwick.

Passengers were immediately placed on Sydney time on boarding, with dinner served shortly after departure despite taking off on Friday morning.



The instructions were to get to sleep as quickly as possible on the first leg of the flight, before players were allowed to disembark their flight at Sri Lanka for a stretching session, though only as far as across the jet bridge and into the gate.

While some will have struggled, the plan clearly worked with some players reporting sleeping 10 hours on their first night after landing on the other side of the world.



AUSSIE RULES

XABI ALONSO was surprised to find out that Chelsea had their own Aussie connection in the squad when touching down.

The Blues named 16-year-old Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli as part of their travelling squad for their pre-season tour, which begins in the city where he was born.

A midfielder, Nicoll-Jazuli was born in Sydney to an Australian mother and a Sudanese father, but spent most of his childhood in England and represents the Three Lions at youth level.

Both Alonso and senior teammates have been impressed with what they have seen from the youngster, who can represent five nations (Australia, Chad, England, France and Sudan) at international level, in training so far.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Nicoll-Jazuli has already agreed scholarship terms with Chelsea ahead of his 17th birthday next January.

It will be a special moment should the midfielder get a chance to play in the city of his birth, but anyone watching on from Football Australia will only have half-hearted interest.

Despite having an international claim to the academy ace, figures within the Socceroos governing body know there is little chance of convincing him to pick a green and gold shirt over either England or France.

Asked about Nicoll-Jazuli, Alonso said: “He has a great dynamism, he has quality, very complete player. He can pass short, he can dribble in the middle, so he has made a good impression so far.



“He’s a talent that we need to help, we need to develop because he has special qualities that you don’t see that often from a 16-year-old guy.”

SEA YOU AGAIN

THERE was a rather awkward note in the air when Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was reunited with his former boss Roberto De Zerbi on the Sydney shoreline.

In the shadow of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, Sanchez, along with Blues manager Xabi Alonso was presented with De Zerbi and Spurs defender Micky van de Ven to mark the start of the Sydney Super Cup pre-season tournament.

Organisers Down Under can probably be forgiven for not twigging that, while Sanchez was at Brighton, he was effectively demoted from first choice to third by the Italian manager. Hardly a happy reunion.



NEW BLUES

CHELSEA are anticipating that a few more players will be added to their tour squad when they land in Hong Kong this weekend.

Nicolas Jackson was slated to be one of those joining up, though his future now looks increasingly uncertain thanks to a veteran Brighton striker.

Danny Welbeck‘s pending arrival – and it has not been ruled out that the former England man could join the squad in Asia if things move quickly enough – has pushed Jackson closer to the exit door.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Aston Villa have opened talks over a £65million deal and the Senegal international, who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich, is now expected to depart.



The same can be said for Spanish forward Marc Guiu, while Liam Delap‘s future is increasingly in doubt.

Sports.title: ‘Absolute joke’ – Man Utd fans fume after finding out club are ready to sell academy graduate, 19, for just £6million
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans have hit back at reports the club is only demanding a few million pounds for one of their top prospects.

And many are even more perplexed by the fact the youngster plays in a position United are actively looking to strengthen this summer.



Harry Amass, 19, got a run in the Red Devils side under Ruben Amorim, playing seven senior games for the club before gaining further experience on loan in the Championship last season.

But according to The Athletic, United are ready to auction him off for just £6million.



Amass has impressed during pre-season and a selection of second-tier clubs are interested in signing him.

The defender scored in last week’s 5-0 friendly win over Rosenborg and played 21 first-team games for Sheffield Wednesday last term, before a subsequent loan stint at Norwich was ruined by injury.

Luke Shaw is United’s only natural left-back aside from Amass, with Patrick Dorgu playing further forward under boss Michael Carrick.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can deputise there but prefer to play on the right.

Lewis Hall and Antonee Robinson are both transfer targets for United – but both would cost several times more than the £6m asking price pinned to Amass.

So the teenager’s cheap valuation has not gone down well with supporters.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

One wrote on X: “This is an absolute joke. Stupid management. How can you plan to sell this emerging talent and buy a 35-40m LB?”

Another moaned: “Selling a prospect for £6m? What’s wrong with them?”

A third ranted: “We don’t have defenders and we are selling the ones we are managing.”

And a fourth chimed in with: “He shouldn’t be going anywhere for less than 15-20m.”

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane, 54, confirmed as France boss replacing Deschamps for first job in FIVE YEARS since Real Madrid exit
Sports.content:
ZINEDINE ZIDANE has finally been appointed as the new France boss after replacing Didier Deschamps.

The former Real Madrid boss returns to football following five years out of the game and will look to rebuild the team after their World Cup semi-final exit.



He takes over from his former France team-mate Deschamps, who spent 14 years with Les Bleus and led them to World Cup glory in 2018.

Zidane joining France was one of the worst kept secrets in football but the French Federation have now confirmed his arrival.



A statement on the official Equipe de France account on X wrote: “ZINEDINE ZIDANE, NEW [MANAGER] OF THE FRENCH NATIONAL TEAM.”

The 54-year-old – who hasn’t coached since leaving Madrid in 2021 – was unveiled at a special press conference on Tuesday morning.

He said it was a “great source of pride” to take the job of his national team.

Zidane added: “I’ve often said it: there’s nothing greater than the French national team.

“So it’s a joy and obviously a great source of pride to become the manager of this French national team.

“It’s also a responsibility. I want to thank [French Football Federation] president Philippe Diallo, the executive committee, and the French Football Federation for their confidence and acknowledge the 14 years of service from Didier and his staff.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I also have a special thought today for all my coaches. Needless to say, I have high ambitions for the French national team.”

He also revealed he turned down many job offers during his five-year hiatus because he was holding out for the France gig.

He added: “I am truly happy. I am ready for the challenge, it motivates me. The only thing I wanted to do after my experience at Real Madrid.

“I have known it since I was a child, I started in the youth teams, I went through every stage until reaching the senior national team, the pinnacle.



“The only thing that motivates me is being able to work for this team and see them continue to win.

“Leading France is the only thing I wanted to do after my experience at Real Madrid. I turned down offers to be the France head coach.”



French football president Philippe Diallo added: “This is an exceptional moment. It has been 14 years since the federation was in a position to appoint a new head coach.

“I would like to say a word for Deschamps: for 14 years he took the France national team to the top. He restored the image of Les Bleus on the pitch. It is important that his work is recognised.”

Zidane – who will start preparing for Euro 2028 in the UK and Ireland – is seen as one of the world’s best managers despite his lengthy absence from top level football.

He won THREE Champions League titles in a row during his time with Los Blancos, as well as two La Liga crowns, two UEFA Super Cups and two Club World Cup trophies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And he wasn’t a bad player either after winning the World Cup with France in 1998 – and was awarded the Ballon d’Or in the same year.



He also won the Champions League with Madrid in 2003, but his career ended in turmoil after infamously headbutting Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final.

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck told to ‘ignore’ Chelsea transfer approach and rejoin Man Utd by club legend
Sports.content:
RIO FERDINAND has made a desperate plea for Danny Welbeck to seal a shock return to Manchester United instead of joining Chelsea.

The striker, 35, narrowly missed out on a place in England’s World Cup squad after bagging 13 Premier League goals for Brighton last season.



And Welbeck’s form has resulted in Chelsea holding talks over a summer switch to Stamford Bridge.

But the prolific marksman has been urged by former United team-mate Ferdinand to snub the West Londoners.



The Red Devils legend, 47, wants Welbeck to head back to Old Trafford if he quits Brighton.

In a social media post, Ferdinand wrote: “Welbs…. Ignore + come back home! Champions League football next season in Manchester.”



Chelsea are eyeing a deal for Welbeck after ripping up their transfer strategy.

The Blues are looking to add more experience to their squad after previously only focusing on landing up-and-coming gems.

Xabi Alonso’s push for wiser heads has resulted in Jordan Henderson joining Welbeck on Chelsea’s wishlist.

But United have prioritised stocking up their options in the middle of the park instead of trying to make Ferdinand’s wish a reality.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

New Red Devils chief Michael Carrick splashed £50million to recruit Andrey Santos from Chelsea.

And the midfielder was quickly followed through the door by Youri Tielemans.

That £35m deal, thanks to triggering a release clause written into the Belgian’s contract at Aston Villa, came 24 hours after goalkeeper Karl Darlow’s arrival.

United already have Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee as forward options.



And that has led to Carrick being more determined to strengthen other positions.

Welbeck notched 29 goals in a trophy-laden spell for United, after coming through the ranks.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans fume at state of pitch for Western Sydney Wanderers friendly as they fear pre-season injuries
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans are scared for their first live pre-season clash after seeing the state of the pitch.

Xabi Alonso has taken his side to Western Sydney Wanderers and the Accor Stadium – but pics of the ground are worrying many.



Patchy grass is seen across the pitch at the home of rugby league outfit South Sydney Rabbitohs and Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs.

New South Wales Blues have also played there with Australia‘s national rugby matches also featured on occasion.



Multi-sports markings were still visible on the pitch ahead of kick-off on Tuesday morning.

Three games were played at the arena over the weekend – and Chelsea trained elsewhere in preparation.

Nervous supporters, who may well remember star Christopher Nkunku going down in the last game of Mauricio Pochettino‘s 2023 summer tour of America, are praying for no injuries.

One wrote on X: “The pitch in Sydney doesn’t look good at all. Chelsea players need to be extra careful on this pitch”.

Another added: “I hope this pitch is injury free”.

A third said: “Why are they using it?! Before the guys will start getting injured”.

The Sun’s Chelsea YouTube channel will be your go-to destination for the latest news, transfer updates, match previews, post-match analysis, exclusive interviews, fan reactions, and breaking stories from Stamford Bridge. Subscribe to The Chelsea Blueprint on YouTube now

Someone else commented: “hopefully no one get injured. No complaints even if we play only academy and squad fringe players.”

Three years ago, in the last match before the Prem started, Nkunku went down against Borussia Dortmund and busted his knee.

It came just days after an Ed Sheeran concert had been hosted on the same pitch and left Chelsea fans reeling.

Nkunku hardly featured under Poch due to the injury and never truly recovered.

Alonso will be desperate to avoid any repeats with a clash against Tottenham at the same ground to come on Saturday.



Chelsea then travel to Hong Kong for the second leg of their tour with games against Juventus, AC Milan, and Johor Darul Ta’zim.

They end back at Stamford Bridge against Alonso’s former club Real Sociedad.

The Blues won both behind-closed-doors friendlies against EFL opponents Crawley and Bromley before heading to the other side of the world.

Sports.title: Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks
Sports.content:
Man Utd stance on hijacking Chelsea's Danny Welbeck transfer after secret talks

Danny Welbeck is in talks to join Chelsea from Brighton in a shock move and Manchester United have also previously considered re-signing their former academy striker

View 2 Images Manchester United have previously made moves to re-sign Danny Welbeck (Image: GLYN KIRK, AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United have given no indication that they are considering a fresh attempt to re-sign Danny Welbeck, who is in talks to sign for Chelsea.

‌



The 35-year-old striker is a United academy graduate who went on to represent the club in the Premier League before joining Arsenal in 2014 for £16million. Welbeck has spent the last six years at Brighton, scoring 23 league goals in the last two seasons for the Seagulls.

‌



Welbeck's fine form last season, plus his wealth of top-flight experience and leadership qualities, has seen him emerge as a surprise transfer target for Chelsea, who are looking to bolster their squad ahead of the new season.

‌



The Blues and Brighton are currently in talks over a deal for Welbeck, whose contract on the south coast expires next year.

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Intriguingly, Manchester United are also in the market for a striker this summer. However, there is nothing to currently suggest they have designs on hijacking Chelsea's move for Welbeck, according to The Athletic.

United have, though, held discussions with Welbeck about a romantic return to Old Traffic in both 2024 and 2025. It's even claimed that talks to bring the veteran back home got 'quite far' last year, with United eventually signing Benjamin Sesko to bolster their attack.

‌



View 2 Images Chelsea are currently in talks to sign Welbeck from Brighton (Image: Izzy Poles/AMA)

Interest in Welbeck comes off the back of his impact since joining Brighton, who qualified for the Europa Conference League last season. Welbeck was their top scorer in the Premier League, plundering 13 goals.

After narrowly missing out on a place in England's World Cup squad, Welbeck is viewed by Chelsea as a quality support option for their first-choice striker, Joao Pedro. Welbeck played with the Brazilian previously at Brighton and would become the eighth player to move between the clubs in recent years if a transfer is finalised.

Article continues below

As well as their pursuit of Welbeck, Chelsea are also working on a deal to sign the veteran midfielder, Jordan Henderson, from Brentford on a free transfer. The 36-year-old still has a year left on the contract he signed when he joined the Bees last summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision
Sports.content:
Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision

Paris Saint-Germain are open to selling Bradley Barcola and Liverpool's chances of signing him have received a boost thanks to Arsenal's fresh stance on the player

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is a top target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Arsenal are not actively pursuing Bradley Barcola, giving Liverpool a free run at signing him. Barcola, 23, has been of interest to both Premier League clubs throughout the summer transfer window, with Paris Saint-Germain open to a sale.

‌



PSG would demand an eye-watering £145million for the winger, who was in and out of France's starting line-up at the World Cup. Liverpool made him a top target and have now been boosted in their pursuit after Arsenal decided to prioritise a stunning move for Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Athletic report that Arsenal's focus is firmly on Real Madrid star, who has one year left on his £400,000-a-week contract. A deal for Barcola is therefore unlikely unless Vinicius snubs the Gunners.

‌



But even with Arsenal out of the picture, Liverpool appear to be reluctant to shell out a club-record fee for Barcola. PSG's argument is that Barcola is worth considerably more than Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, who Manchester City and Chelsea respectively have paid £116m and £117m for this summer.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

The Frenchman's stock is also high thanks to helping Luis Enrique's side win back-to-back Champions Leagus and having come through Barcelona's famous academy. Enrique is said to only want players who are committed to PSG, plunging Barcola's future into uncertainty.

‌



Barcola himself doesn't know the answer, having been asked about the prospect of a transfer earlier this month. "I'm focused on the World Cup," the 23-year-old said. "What happens after that, I don't know."

Should Liverpool pay £145million for Bradley Barcola? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's future at Paris Saint-Germain is uncertain (Image: Franco Arland/Getty Images)

‌



New manager Andoni Iraola has admitted that Liverpool 'definitely need to sign a winger', having been asked about the Reds' transfer plans last week. "When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola explained.

"There are obvious situations where we need to sign players. Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."

Liverpool will kick-off their Premier League campaign and new era under Iraola away to Newcastle on Sunday, August 23. The Reds have played one pre-season friendly so far, beating Sunderland 4-2.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah transfer at risk of collapse as new club enters race for Liverpool legend

Mohamed Salah had been in talks with Besiktas over a move to the Turkish club but one of their senior figures has delivered a damning update on his potential transfer move

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah was planning to leave last summer before signing a new deal (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Besiktas have claimed they've walked away from talks to sign Mohamed Salah despite several meetings with the former Liverpool man.

‌



The Egyptian is a free agent after being allowed to leave Anfield a year before the end of his contract and, now 34, the forward is looking for a new club, with the Turkish side believing they were leading the race.

‌



Salah had been the subject of approach from Besiktas with the club's president Serdal Adali telling Turkish media they were awaiting a final decision, but director Onder Ozen has claimed they have hit a roadblock with communications coming to a stand still.

‌



He believes Salah's representatives are in talks with another club but insists their final offer remains on the table if they want to make the move happen.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems READ MORE :

Ozen told Turkish media: "We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model. Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

"Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21st onwards. Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process. I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this.

‌



"The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there. I don't have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas's offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated.

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah left Liverpool at the end of last season (Image: Getty Images)

"But Besiktas will not make another offer. They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there. The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas's club identity."

Article continues below

Besiktas have just signed Leandro Trossard from Arsenal as they look to bolster their ranks ahead of the upcoming season. Whilst being competitive they've not claimed the Turkish title since 2021 with Galatasaray the dominant force currently.

Salah will not be without options has long been linked with a move to Saudi Arabia with Liverpool turning down lucrative offers in the past whilst the MLS also remains a possibility if the ex-Red wants to see out his playing days in the United States.

Sports.title: Thierry Henry slammed Jose Mourinho for treatment of Vinicius Jr as Arsenal move arises
Sports.content:
Thierry Henry slammed Jose Mourinho for treatment of Vinicius Jr as Arsenal move arises

Arsenal legend Thierry Henry could barely contain his fury at Jose Mourinho after a row erupted around the manager's behaviour toward Gunners target Vinicius Jr

View 2 Images Arsenal legend Thierry Henry fumed at Jose Mourinho for his reaction to the Vinicius Jr racism storm in February (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Vinicius Jr's surprise links to Arsenal this summer will be of major interest to Gunners icon Thierry Henry. And the Frenchman may be eager to see "the best left winger in the world" arrive at the Emirates Stadium for more reasons than one.

‌



Vinicius, 26, has emerged as a surprise target for Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta after entering the final 12 months of his contract in Madrid. There's a fine chance the Brazilian's representatives are simply using rumours as bait to land an even better deal for their client, though the powers that be in north London will hope there's a genuine chance of acquiring his signature.

‌



And one would forgive Vinicius for feeling some angst about the idea of playing under Mourinho. This comes after Henry failed to hide his frustrations at 'The Special One' for his refusal to call out alleged racism aimed at Vinicius.

‌



The incident unfolded this past February when Real met Benfica, then managed by Mourinho, in the knockout play-offs of the Champions League. Vinicius scored the only goal of the game at the Estadio da Luz and soon appealed to the referee, accusing Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni of aiming racist abuse at him.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Argentinian Prestianni, who was later banned over the incident, pulled his jersey up to cover his mouth before clearly saying something in Vinicius' direction. The winger sat in the dugout as the game was paused for 10 minutes, then he was subject to a chorus of boos from the Benfica fanbase whenever he received the ball once the game resumed.

‌



Jose Mourinho breaks silence after criticism over Vinicius Junior incident with Benfica vow READ MORE :

FIFA president says players who cover their mouths could be sent off in new rule READ MORE :

Mourinho, 63, was criticised for his response to the alleged racism and instead put the responsibility on Vinicius for not celebrating his goal respectfully enough. He went on to say he "didn't believe" Vinicius or Prestianni because they each told him different things, though his comments didn't wash with Henry.

"I can relate to what Vinicius is going through. That happened to me so many times on the pitch," said the Arsenal icon during the CBS broadcast. "I talked about it so many times after games. I’ve also been accused of looking for excuses after games when that happened to me. At times, you feel lonely, because it’s going to be your word against his word.

"We don’t know what Prestianni has said, because he was very courageous by putting his shirt over his mouth to make sure that we weren’t going to see what he said. So clearly, already, you look suspicious.

‌



View 2 Images Gianluca Prestianni, who has been accused of racist comments in the past, appeared to say something offensive to Real star Vinicius Jr (Image: Getty Images)

"Because you didn’t want people to see or read what you said. Then, the reaction of Vinicius is telling me that something not right happened. We still don’t know what was said."

Henry put the responsibility squarely on Benfica's players and fans, as well as Mourinho, for their own actions. And he criticised the new Real manager, who has returned to their helm after almost a decade away, for deflecting attention off his player in such a serious situation.

‌



"I wanted to know what his player said," Henry continued. "He deflected the subject for us to talk about something else. He’s very good at that. The game didn’t stop because of the celebration, the game stopped because of what Prestianni apparently said."

Vinicius may have his own feelings about playing under Mourinho after that debacle. The coach would be wise to ensure he achieves a resolution with arguably Real's most valuable player, with Arsenal among those reportedly willing to capitalise if that isn't the case.

Reports have indicated Los Blancos have offered their forward a new contract worth somewhere around £325,000 a week. That's more than Arsenal's highest earner, Bukayo Saka, currently earns after penning new terms worth £300,000 a week.

Sports.title: 'I was set to join Real Madrid but Liverpool boss rang and I joined them instead'
Sports.content:
'I was set to join Real Madrid but Liverpool boss rang and I joined them instead'

A personal phone call convinced a promising young talent to snub Real Madrid in favour of Liverpool

View 2 Images Liverpool hijacked Suso's move to Real Madrid in 2010 (Image: Tom Szczerbowski, Getty Images)

Liverpool beat Real Madrid to the signing of exciting young winger Suso in stunning fashion 16 years ago. The Spaniard had already agreed personal terms with Los Blancos but a phone call from then Reds manager Rafael Benitez changed everything.

‌



Now, almost two decades later, the roles have reversed, with Real Madrid set to get the better of Liverpool by striking a deal to land Yan Diomande. The La Liga giants agreed personal terms with the 19-year-old RB Leipzig winger on the weekend.

‌



Diomande had been Liverpool’s top transfer target for much of this summer, with the Reds having an initial £85million bid rejected for the Ivory Coast international last month. That fell short of Leipzig’s valuation and PSG soon moved ahead in the race for his signature, given the player’s reported preference to join the Parisians.

‌



However, PSG also failed to meet the asking price, allowing Real Madrid to hijack the deal with a reported offer of over £100m. PSG have refused to enter a bidding war after having a final bid rejected for the teenager on Sunday, while Liverpool have moved on to other targets, such as PSG’s Bradley Barcola, seemingly ending the tug of war for the player.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Diomande may have opted for the Bernabeu over Merseyside, but Suso back in 2010 saw Anfield as the better destination for his development. The Reds completed the signing back in the summer of 2010 from his hometown club Cadiz.

‌



Suso, then merely a teenager, initially joined on loan until he was old enough to obtain a work permit to play professionally. He later explained that Benitez, Liverpool's manager at the time, persuaded him to make the move to Anfield that summer, despite the player being on the verge of joining the La Liga giants after they had tabled a substantial offer for him.

View 2 Images Real Madrid look set to sign Liverpool target Yan Diomande (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Benitez, himself Spanish, sat down with the player and his family to sell Liverpool's vision, while also making it clear just how highly he rated the young Spaniard. He succeeded in convincing Suso to turn his back on Madrid in favour of Liverpool, though Benitez would leave Anfield by mutual consent that very same summer on June 3, meaning Suso never actually featured under the manager who signed him.

‌



Suso later told Cope: "I had agreed on a contract with Real Madrid, and the transfer was basically done, but then Rafael Benitez called me and told me he had a lot of confidence in me and that I should go to Liverpool. I'm glad I made this decision. I love this club and it is the best for me."

Suso put pen to paper on his first professional contract on his 17th birthday in November 2010. He went on to develop through Liverpool's youth ranks and reserves before earning his breakthrough under Brendan Rodgers during the 2012/13 campaign.
